introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.p: ISO 10303 is an International Standard for the computer-interpretable representation of product information and for the exchange of product data. The objective is to provide a neutral mechanism capable of describing products throughout their life cycle. This mechanism is suitable not only for neutral file exchange, but also as a basis for implementing and sharing product databases, and as a basis for retention and archiving.
Major subdivisions of this part of ISO 10303 are:

The generic product description resources provide an overall organization for the integrated resources that are documented in other parts of ISO 10303. They specify resource constructs that provide consistent representation of facts about products in different application-specific views.

The generic management resources support the description of information that is used to manage and control product data. Together, the generic product description resources and the generic management resources are the foundations upon which application interpreted models, the normative conceptual schemas of application protocols, are built. Application interpreted models specialize selected generic management resources to elements of the integrated product description resources to satisfy the requirements that are specified in the application reference model.
The support resources are a set of shared resource constructs that are used by the ISO 10303 integrated resources. They provide an underlying consistency across the resources of ISO 10303.

In this International Standard, the same English language words may be used to refer to an object in the real world or concept, and as the name of an EXPRESS data type that represents this object or concept. The following typographical convention is used to distinguish between these. If a word or phrase occurs in the same typeface as narrative text, the referent is the object or concept. If the word or phrase occurs in a bold typeface, the referent is the EXPRESS data type. Names of EXPRESS schemas also occur in a bold typeface.

The name of an EXPRESS data type may be used to refer to the data type itself, or to an instance of the data type. The distinction between these uses is normally clear from the context. If there is a likelihood of ambiguity, either the phrase “entity data type” or “instance(s) of” is included in the text.
Double quotation marks (“”) denote quoted text. Single quotation marks (‘’) denote particular text string values.

clause.title: General
clause.p: {% assign docname = sdi | replace: “_”, ” ” %} {% case term sdt not resolved via ID sdt %} {% when “aic” %} This part of ISO 10303 specifies the interpretation of the integrated resources to satisfy requirements for the representation of term docname not resolved via ID docname. {% when “igr” %} This part of ISO 10303 specifies the integrated generic resource constructs for term docname not resolved via ID docname. {% when “iar” %} This part of ISO 10303 specifies the integrated application resource constructs for term docname not resolved via ID docname. {% endcase %} —-
The schemas that are specified in this part of ISO 10303 are organized as follows.

clause.title: Generic product description resources
clause.p: This part of ISO 10303 specifies the resource constructs for the high level structure for the representation of products and their properties. It also specifies ISO 10303 integrated resources for the description of generic aspects of product usage, categorization of products and associations between products.
The following are within scope in this part of ISO 10303:

li.p: the characterization of a product in one or more application contexts;
the definition of relationships among products;
the identification of the properties of a product or of a portion of a product;
the identification of a representation of a property;

example.p: A 3D geometric model or a table of numerical values are different representations of properties of a product.

li.p: the description of the application context for which product data is defined.

clause.title: Generic management resources
clause.p: This part of ISO 1030 specifies the resource constructs to associate administrative data with product data.
The following are within scope in this part of ISO 10303:

li.p: the structure for associating product data with related administrative data.

clause.title: Support resources
clause.p: This part of ISO 10303 specifies the resource constructs for administrative data, physical quantities and their units, and basic data types.
The identification and description of following are within scope in this part of ISO 10303:

li.p: the actions, action requests, and the status of actions;
the certification, approvals, security classifications, and effectivities;
the specification of dates and times;
the provision of mechanisms for grouping items and referring to information that is defined outside an exchange;
the physical quantities and their units;
the provision of mechanisms to define values for id, name, description and role attributes;
the location of a person, organization, or product;
the experience, qualifications, and position in an organization of a person.

verbal-definition.p: result of discussions between the partners of product data exchange or sharing that ensures that all of them have the same understanding of the transferred or shared information

semx.p: result of discussions between the partners of product data exchange or sharing that ensures that all of them have the same understanding of the transferred or shared information

termnote.p: The agreement may be formalized in a document.

verbal-definition.p: EXPRESS schema for which a natural language definition is given with each CONSTANT, TYPE, ENTITY, RULE, FUNCTION or PROCEDURE construct

semx.p: EXPRESS schema for which a natural language definition is given with each CONSTANT, TYPE, ENTITY, RULE, FUNCTION or PROCEDURE construct

termexample.p: Clause 5.2 of an application protocol contains an annotated EXPRESS schema.

verbal-definition.p: path in which all nodes and links are distinct

semx.p: path in which all nodes and links are distinct

verbal-definition.p: set of all products satisfying a type of product; the elements of the set are referred to as members of the class

semx.p: set of all products satisfying a type of product; the elements of the set are referred to as members of the class

termnote.p: A class need not have any members.
The definition of the type will determine whether the size of the set varies with time.
This definition was adapted from ISO/IEC 10746-2:1996 [1].

verbal-definition.p: number of direct connections to other nodes

semx.p: number of direct connections to other nodes

verbal-definition.p: Information required for proper control and handling of a specific product or item.

semx.p: Information required for proper control and handling of a specific product or item.

termexample.p: An inspection certification indicates that the product has passed inspection and is ready to move to the next step in the product life cycle.

termnote.p: Management data may include information related to scheduling, roles, certifications, approvals, effectivity and life-cycle stages.

verbal-definition.p: a sequence of nodes such that from each of itse nodes thre is an edge to the next node in the sequence; it has two terminal nodes (nodes that have degree 1), while all others (if any) have degree 2

semx.p: a sequence of nodes such that from each of itse nodes thre is an edge to the next node in the sequence; it has two terminal nodes (nodes that have degree 1), while all others (if any) have degree 2

termnote.p: The first and last nodes in the path are different. No nodes are referenced more than once by a link.

verbal-definition.p: object that exists or did exist in the real world and that can or could be uniquely identified

semx.p: object that exists or did exist in the real world and that can or could be uniquely identified

termexample.p: The Moon is an individual object that is not the result of a human process.

termnote.p: An individual object may result from a manufacturing process or it may exist independently of any human process.

verbal-definition.p: predicate characterizing a collection of products; a product is of the type, or satisfies the type, if the predicate holds for that product

semx.p: predicate characterizing a collection of products; a product is of the type, or satisfies the type, if the predicate holds for that product

termexample.p: This definition was adapted from ISO/IEC 10746-2:1996 [1].

verbal-definition.p: a unique revision of an item

semx.p: a unique revision of an item

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the action_schema is the description of actions, the reasons for these actions, and the status of these actions.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the action_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 2 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Action information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: as_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The as_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: as_id_attribute_select
clause.p: The as_id_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: as_name_attribute_select
clause.p: The as_name_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: as_role_select
clause.p: The as_role_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: supported_item
clause.p: The supported_item type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The supported_item allows for the designation of an action_directiveaction_directive, an actionaction, or an action_methodaction_method.

clause.title: action
clause.p: An action is the identification of the occurrence of an activity and a description of its result.
An action identifies an activity that has taken place, is taking place, or is expected to take place in the future.
An action has a definition that is specified by an action_methodaction_method.
name: the labellabel by which the action is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
chosen_method: the action_methodaction_method that specifies the procedure selected to carry out the action and a description of the results of that action.
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the action.
WR1: Each action shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.

clause.title: action_directive
clause.p: An action_directive is an authoritative instrument that provides directions to achieve the specified results.
name: the labellabel by which the action_directive is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_directive. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

analysis: an informal description of the results of the analysis that was carried out on the elements of the requests set. The request sets are the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_requests referenced in the requests attribute.
comment: an informal description of any other pertinent information.
requests: a set of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request entity data types that defines the expected results.

clause.title: action_method
clause.p: An action_method is the definition of an activity. This definition includes the activity’s objectives and effects.
name: the labellabel by which the action_method is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_method. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
consequence: an informal description of the effects of the action_method.
purpose: an informal description of the objectives of the action_method.

clause.title: action_method_relationship
clause.p: An action_method_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_methodaction_method and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
name: the labellabel by which the action_method_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_method_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
relating_method: one of the instances of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship.

related_method: the other instance of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: action_relationship
clause.p: An action_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type actionaction and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
name: the labellabel by which the action_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
relating_action: one of the instances of actionaction that is a part of the relationship.
related_action: the other instance of actionaction that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: action_request_solution
clause.p: An action_request_solution is an association between a versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request and an action_methodaction_method that is a potential solution for the request.
method: the action_methodaction_method that is a potential solution.
request: the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request for which a solution is specified.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_request_solution.
name: the labellabel by which the action_request_solution is known.
WR1: Each action_request_solution shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.
WR2: Each action_request_solution shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.

clause.title: action_request_status
clause.p: An action_request_status is the association of a status with a versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request.
status: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.
assigned_request: the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request to which the status applies.

clause.title: action_resource
clause.p: An action_resource is a thing that is identified as being needed to carry out an action.
name: the labellabel by which the action_resource is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_resource. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
usage: a set of supported_itemsupported_items for which the action_resource is used.
kind: the action_resource_typeaction_resource_type that specifies the sort of action_resource that is being used.

clause.title: action_resource_relationship
clause.p: An action_resource_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_resourceaction_resource and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
name: the labellabel by which the action_resource_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the action_resource_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
relating_resource: one of the instances of action_resourceaction_resource that is a part of the relationship.

related_resource: the other instance of action_resourceaction_resource that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: action_resource_type
clause.p: An action_resource_type is the identification of the kind of action_resourceaction_resource needed to carry out an action.
name: the labellabel by which the action_resource_type is known.

clause.title: action_status
clause.p: An action_status is the association of a status with an executed_actionexecuted_action.
status: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.
assigned_action: the executed_actionexecuted_action to which the status applies.

clause.title: directed_action
clause.p: A directed_action is a type of executed_actionexecuted_action that is governed by an action_directiveaction_directive.
directive: the action_directiveaction_directive that governs the directed_action.

clause.title: directed_action_assignment
clause.p: A directed_action_assignment is an association of a directed_actiondirected_action with product data.
assigned_directed_action: the instance of the directed_action entity data that is to be associated with product data.
role: the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the directed_action_assignment with product data.
WR1: Each directed_action_assignment shall be item_with_role in at most one role_associationrole_association.

clause.title: executed_action
clause.p: An executed_action is a type of actionaction that is completed, partially completed, or just identified. It may but need not have status information associated with it.

clause.title: versioned_action_request
clause.p: A versioned_action_request is a specification of a desired result.
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request.
version: the identification of the version of the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
purpose: an informal description of the reason for the versioned_action_request.
description: the texttext that characterizes the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: versioned_action_request_relationship
clause.p: A versioned_action_request_relationship is a relationship between two versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request objects.
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request_relationship.
name: the labellabel by which the versioned_action_request_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the versioned_action_request_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
relating_versioned_action_request: one of the instances of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship.

related_versioned_action_request: the other instance of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: action_directive_relationship
clause.p: An action_directive_relationship is a relationship between two action_directiveaction_directive objects.
name: shall be unique within a population of action_directive_relationship.
description: the text or the set of texts that provide further information about the action_directive_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
relating: one object of action_directiveaction_directive that is part of the relationship.
related: the other object of action_directiveaction_directive that is part of the relationship.
relation_type: the meaning of the relationship.
WR1: A action_directive_relationship shall not participate in its own definition.

clause.title: acyclic_action_method_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_action_method_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type action_methodaction_method that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an action_method_relationshipaction_method_relationship or any of its subtypes.
The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
relation: (input) the candidate action_method_relationshipaction_method_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type action_methodaction_method that the function is searching for in the relating_methodrelating_method parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the action_method_relationshipaction_method_relationship entity.

relation: (input) the candidate action_relationshipaction_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type actionaction for which the function is searching in the relating_actionrelating_action parameter of the relation argument.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the application_context_schema is the applicable usages of product data. This schema provides a mechanism for application protocols to define a frame of reference or context that applies to particular sets of product data.
This schema also provides a means to identify application protocols.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the application_context_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 3 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The meaningful exchange of product data requires the identification of the application context in which that product data is defined. An application context may have several context elements. Each context element may be referenced by a different set of product data.

clause.title: acs_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The acs_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: acs_id_attribute_select
clause.p: The acs_id_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: exchange_identification_context_select
clause.p: The exchange_identification_context_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The exchange_identification_context_select type allows for the designation of the data types identification_assignmentidentification_assignment and organizationorganization .

clause.title: application_context
clause.p: An application_context, as defined in ISO 10303-1, is a context in which product data is defined and has meaning. An application_context represents various types of information that relate to product data and may affect the meaning and usage of that data.

application: the labellabel by which the application_context is known.NOTE 1Note 15.4.1, Note 1
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

description: the texttext that characterizes the application_context.NOTE 2Note 25.4.1, Note 2
The description attribute aids in defining the usage of product data in an application_context. NOTE 3Note 35.4.1, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the application_context.NOTE 4Note 45.4.1, Note 4
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994. NOTE 5Note 55.4.1, Note 5
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
context_elements: the set of instances of the entity data type application_context_elementapplication_context_element that defines the various aspects of the application_context.

WR1: Each application_context shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 6Note 65.4.1, Note 6
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

WR2: Each application_context shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.NOTE 7Note 75.4.1, Note 7
The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 8Note 85.4.1, Note 8
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: application_context_element
clause.p: An application_context_element is an aspect of an application context that contains information about the context in which product data is defined. This aspect contains information about the conditions in which the product data exists.

An application_context_element may be either a library_contextlibrary_context or a product_concept_contextproduct_concept_context, or a product_contextproduct_context, or a product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context.
name: the labellabel by which the application_context_element is known.

example.p: ‘Functional definition’, ‘physical definition’, ‘usage occurrence’, and ‘manufacturable definition’ are examples of names.

clause.p: frame_of_reference: the application_contextapplication_context of which this application_context_element is a member.

clause.title: application_context_relationship
clause.p:
An application_context_relationship is a relationship between two instances of application_contextapplication_context and provides a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 15.4.3, Note 1
The role of application_context_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 25.4.3, Note 2
Without any further specialization, this relationship does not imply that the product data associated with relating_context are also associated with the related_context. NOTE 3Note 35.4.3, Note 3
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 4Note 45.4.3, Note 4
This entity, together with the application_contextapplication_context entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the application_context_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the application_context_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_context: one of the instances of application_contextapplication_context that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 5Note 55.4.3, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_context: the other instance of application_contextapplication_context that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 6Note 65.4.3, Note 6
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: application_protocol_definition
clause.p: An application_protocol_definition is the identification of an application protocol.
status: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the application protocol.

example.p: “IS”, “DIS”, “TS” or “CD” are examples of application protocol states.

clause.p: application_interpreted_model_schema_name: the EXPRESS schema name of the application interpreted model.
application_protocol_year: the year when the application protocol attained the status given by the status attribute.
application: the application context of the application protocol.

clause.title: library_context
clause.p: A library_context is a type of application_context_elementapplication_context_element that defines a context for elements of a library.

The inherited attribute namename identifies or characterizes the type of library.NOTENote5.4.5, Note
The name attribute can represent the nature of the source of the library, the nature of the contents of the library, or both.

example.p: ‘Dewey Decimal’, ‘ISO 13584 library’, and ‘supplier catalogue’ are examples of type of library.

clause.p: library_reference: the labellabel that identifies the library.

example.p: ‘ACME self-propelled rocket sleds catalogue’ is an example of a library reference.

clause.title: product_concept_context
clause.p: A product_concept_context is a type of application_context_elementapplication_context_element that defines a context for a product_conceptproduct_concept (see ISO 10303-44).
A product_concept_context represents information that relates to the characterization of potential purchasers of a product. Such information may affect the meaning and usage of the product data.
market_segment_type: the labellabel that identifies the kind of consumer preferences associated with a product.

example.p: ‘Luxury automobiles’, ‘laptop personal computers’, and ‘budget personal stereos’ are examples of *market_segment_type*s.

clause.title: product_context
clause.p:
A product_context is a type of application_context_elementapplication_context_element that represents life cycle independent information about a productproduct. This information describes the discipline in which data about the product are created. NOTE 1Note 15.4.7, Note 1
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_context entity data type in order to establish consistency among schemas that relate to the same types or kinds of products.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for design and construction of buildings respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘building’, and the discipline_type attribute to be ‘architecture’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute namename identifies a particular industry, subject area, or kind of product for which product data is created or used.NOTE 2Note 25.4.7, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘ship’, ‘aircraft’ and ‘building’ are examples of names of product contexts.

clause.p:
discipline_type: the labellabel that identifies a particular field of practice involved in creating or using product data.NOTE 3Note 35.4.7, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘electronics’, ‘engineering’, or ‘architecture’ are examples of discipline types.

clause.title: product_definition_context
clause.p:
A product_definition_context is a type of application_context_elementapplication_context_element that represents information about the stage in the product life cycle for which a product_definitionproduct_definition is created or used. NOTE 1Note 15.4.8, Note 1
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_definition_context entity data type in order to maintain consistency between schemas that relate to the same or related life-cycle phases.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for conceptual design and detailed design of process plants respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘conceptual design’ and ‘detailed design’, and the life_cycle_stage attribute to be ‘design’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute namename identifies a subdivision or characterization of a life cycle stage for which product data is created or used.NOTE 2Note 25.4.8, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘required’ and ‘planned’ are examples of names of product definition contexts, used in conjunction with a life cycle stage of ‘thermal analysis’.

clause.p:
life_cycle_stage: the labellabel that identifies a stage in the life cycle of a product.NOTE 3Note 35.4.8, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A ‘preliminary design’ and ‘manufacturing planning’ are examples of life cycle stages.

clause.title: dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context and is an abstract entity that describes a specific context for exchange.

WR1: at least one of the entities identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_contextidentification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context or language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_contextlanguage_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context shall be specified.

clause.title: identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: An identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_contextdependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the context of the product_definitionproduct_definition exchange.
identification_context: specifies the context of the exchange to be either identification_assignmentidentification_assignment or organizationorganization .

clause.title: language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_contextdependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the specified language of the product_definitionproduct_definition exchange context.
language: specifies the default language of the exchange context.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- application_context_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- application_context_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the approval_schema is the description of authorization data. Approval information concerns the acceptance of product data.

example.p: One version of a product may be approved for manufacture whilst another may still be undergoing design.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the approval_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 4 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Approval information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: apps_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The apps_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: apps_role_select
clause.p: The apps_role_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: approval
clause.p:
An approval is a confirmation of the product data for its intended use. An approval is an incompletely modelled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete approval. NOTENote6.4.1, Note
The role of approval can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
status: the type or level of approval in terms of its usage.

example.p: One possible status is ‘released for production’; this explicitly identifies the approved usage. Another possible status is ‘preliminary design completed’; this only implies the approved usage that will depend upon company-specific procedures.

clause.p: level: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the approval.

clause.title: approval_date_time
clause.p: An approval_date_time is an association between an approvalapproval and a date, time, or date and time.
date_time: the moment when the dated_approval is given.
dated_approval: the approvalapproval with which the date or time is associated.

role: the object_roleobject_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the approval_date_time with product data.NOTE 1Note 16.4.2, Note 1
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to approval_date_time as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each approval_date_time shall be the item_with_roleitem_with_role in at most one role_associationrole_association.NOTE 2Note 26.4.2, Note 2
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: approval_person_organization
clause.p: An approval_person_organization is an association between an approvalapproval and a given person, organization, or person in the context of an organization.
person_organization: the person or organization playing the given role.
authorized_approval: the approvalapproval that is affected by the person or organization.
role: the approval_roleapproval_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the approvalapproval with a person or organization.

clause.title: approval_relationship
clause.p:
An approval_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type approvalapproval with a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 16.4.4, Note 1
The role of approval_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 26.4.4, Note 2
This entity, together with the approvalapproval entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the approval_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the approval_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_approval: one of the instances of approvalapproval that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 3Note 36.4.4, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_approval: the other instance of approvalapproval that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 4Note 46.4.4, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: approval_role
clause.p: An approval_role is a definition of a function. An approval_role is an incompletely modelled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete confirmation.

role: the labellabel by which the approval_role is known.NOTE 1Note 16.4.5, Note 1
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

description: the texttext that characterizes the approval_role.NOTE 2Note 26.4.5, Note 2
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to approval_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each approval_role shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 3Note 36.4.5, Note 3
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 4Note 46.4.5, Note 4
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: approval_status
clause.p: An approval_status specifies the state of an approvalapproval.

example.p: ‘Approved’ and ‘disapproved’ are examples of approval_status.

clause.p:
name: the labellabel by which the approval_status is known.NOTENote6.4.6, Note
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: acyclic_approval_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_approval_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type approvalapproval that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a approval_relationshipapproval_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 16.5.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 26.5.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the approval_relationshipapproval_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate approval_relationshipapproval_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type approvalapproval for which the function is searching in the relating_approvalrelating_approval parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the approval_relationshipapproval_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- approval_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- approval_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the basic_attribute_schema is the assignment of id, name, description and role attributes to aspects of product data. This schema defines the mechanism to define a value for these attributes and associate it with product data.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the basic_attribute_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 5 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following concepts are supported by this schema:

li.p: the assignment of an identifier to product data;
the assignment of a label to product data;
the assignment of a descriptive text to product data;
the assignment of a role to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data.

clause.p: The assignment of an identifier corresponds to the id_attribute entity data type. The entities to which an identifier may be assigned are specified in the id_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute id. The corresponding identifier value is provided by the get_id_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of id_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the id_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a name corresponds to the name_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a name may be assigned are specified in the name_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute name. The corresponding label value is provided by the get_name_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of name_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the name_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a descriptive text corresponds to the description_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a description may be assigned are specified in the description_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute description. The corresponding text value is provided by the get_description_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of description_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the description_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a role corresponds to the role_association entity data type. The entities to which a role may be assigned are specified in the role_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute role. The corresponding object_role is provided by the get_role function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of role_association assigned to an instance of an entity in the role_select type.

clause.title: description_attribute_select
clause.p:
The description_attribute_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the description_attribute_select type.NOTENote7.3.1, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
A description_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a descriptive text.

sourcecode.body: TYPE description_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE description_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: generic_attribute_list_select
clause.p:
The generic_attribute_list_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the generic_attribute_list_select type.NOTENote7.3.2, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
A generic_attribute_list_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a generic attribute list.

sourcecode.body: TYPE generic_attribute_list_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE generic_attribute_list_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: generic_attribute_select
clause.p:
The generic_attribute_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the generic_attribute_select type.NOTENote7.3.3, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
A generic_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a generic attribute.

sourcecode.body: TYPE generic_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE generic_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: id_attribute_select
clause.p:
The id_attribute_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the id_attribute_select type.NOTENote7.3.4, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
An id_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned an identifier.

sourcecode.body: TYPE id_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE id_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: name_attribute_select
clause.p:
The name_attribute_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the name_attribute_select type.NOTENote7.3.5, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
A name_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a name.

sourcecode.body: TYPE name_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE name_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: role_select
clause.p:
The role_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the role_select type.NOTENote7.3.6, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.
A role_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a role.

sourcecode.body: TYPE role_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE role_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: aggregate_id_attribute
clause.p: An aggregate_id_attribute is used for the case where there is more than one product data element for a specific identifier.
attribute_value: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the identified_item.
identified_item: the collection of items that are identified.

clause.title: description_attribute
clause.p: A description_attribute is the assignment of a descriptive text string to product data.
attribute_value: the texttext that characterizes the described_item.
described_item: the item that is described.

clause.title: generic_attribute
clause.p: A generic_attribute is the declaration of a named attribute as a text string to enable it to be associated with product data. This capability shall not be used to replace more specific assignment capabilities if both are available to a specified target.
attribute_name: the labellabel used to name the generic_attribute.
attribute_value: the texttext that characterizes the generic_attribute.

clause.title: generic_attribute_assignment
clause.p: A generic_attribute_assignment is the assignment of a generic attribute to element of product data.
attribute: the generic_attributegeneric_attribute to be associated with the product data.
item_with_attribute: the item to which the attribute is assigned.

clause.title: generic_attribute_list_assignment
clause.p: A generic_attribute_list_assignment is the assignment of a named list of generic attributes to element of product data.
attribute_name: the labellabel used to name the list of generic attributes.
attributes: the list of generic_attributegeneric_attributes that are assigned to the element of product data.
item_with_attribute: the item to which the attributes are assigned.

clause.title: id_attribute
clause.p: An id_attribute is the assignment of an identifier to product data.
attribute_value: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the identified_item.
identified_item: the item that is identified.

clause.title: name_attribute
clause.p: A name_attribute is the assignment of a label by which the product data is known.
attribute_value: the labellabel by which the named_item is known.
named_item: the item to which the name is applied.

clause.title: object_role
clause.p: An object_role is a specification of a role for the association of management type data with other aspects of product data and a description of that role.
name: the labellabel by which the object_role is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the object_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: role_association
clause.p: A role_association is the assignment of an object_roleobject_role to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data.
role: the object_roleobject_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the role_association with product data.
item_with_role: the item to which a role is assigned.

clause.title: get_description_value
clause.p: The get_description_value function accepts an object to which a descriptive text string may be assigned and returns this description if present.

If a description_attributedescription_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_valueattribute_value attribute of this description_attributedescription_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.
obj: (input) the object for which a texttext is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.title: get_id_value
clause.p: The get_id_value function accepts an object to which an identifier may be assigned and returns this identifier if present.

If an id_attributeid_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_valueattribute_value attribute of this id_attributeid_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.
obj: (input) the object for which an identifieridentifier is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.title: get_aggregate_id_value
clause.p: The get_aggregate_id_value function accepts an object to which an identifier may be assigned and returns this identifier if present.

If an aggregate_id_attributeaggregate_id_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_valueattribute_value attribute of this aggregate_id_attributeaggregate_id_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.
obj: (input) the object for which an identifieridentifier is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.title: get_name_value
clause.p: The get_name_value function accepts an object to which a label may be assigned and returns this label if present.

If a name_attributename_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_valueattribute_value attribute of this name_attributename_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.
obj: the object for which a labellabel is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.title: get_role
clause.p: The get_role function accepts an object to which a role may be assigned and returns this role if present.

If a role_associationrole_association references the object, the function will return the object_roleobject_role of the rolerole attribute of this role_associationrole_association. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.
obj: (input) the object for which an object_roleobject_role is determined. This is an input to the function.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- basic_attribute_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- basic_attribute_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the certification_schema is the definition of certifications. A certification assures and validates product data.

example.p: A material certificate states the chemical composition of one or more physical pieces of material, for example, purchased raw material. The presence of the material certificate removes the need to test the composition of the material; it allows the specified material composition to be accepted as fact without further investigation.
A certified supplier can supply goods that do not require checking.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the certification_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 6 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Certification information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: certification
clause.p:
A certification is an assertion of facts. A certification is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete certification. NOTENote8.3.1, Note
The role of certification can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the certification is known.
purpose: an informal description of the reason the certification is applied.

example.p: A purpose for material certification could be the fact that certain customers demand material certification for the products that are supplied to them.

clause.p: kind: the certification_typecertification_type that defines the class of certification that is applied.

clause.title: certification_type
clause.p: A certification_type is the kind of certificationcertification granted.

example.p: Suppliers and manufacturers can be certified.

clause.p:
description: the texttext that characterizes the certification_type.NOTENote8.3.2, Note
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A certification type in an example supply chain is ‘supplier’.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- certification_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- certification_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the contract_schema is the description of contract agreements.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the contract_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 7 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Contract information may be attached to any aspect of a product data.

clause.title: contract
clause.p:
A contract is a binding agreement. A contract is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete contract. NOTENote9.3.1, Note
Contracts may be enforceable by law.
name: the labellabel by which the contract is known.
purpose: an informal description of the reason for the contract.
kind: the contract‘s type.

clause.title: contract_relationship
clause.p:
A contract_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type contractcontract. NOTE 1Note 19.3.2, Note 1
The role of contract_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 29.3.2, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 39.3.2, Note 3
This entity, together with the contractcontract entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the contract_relationship.NOTE 4Note 49.3.2, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the contract_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the contract_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_contract: one of the instances of contractcontract that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 5Note 59.3.2, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_contract: the other instance of contractcontract that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 6Note 69.3.2, Note 6
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: contract_type
clause.p: A contract_type is the kind of information that an instance of contractcontract conveys.

example.p: A contract for an organization that is supplying goods to another organization could be ‘fixed’ or ’cost plus’.

clause.p:
description: the texttext that characterizes the contract_type. The value of the attribute need not be specified.NOTENote9.3.3, Note
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: acyclic_contract_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_contract_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type contractcontract that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a contract_relationshipcontract_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 19.4.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 29.4.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the contract_relationshipcontract_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate contract_relationshipcontract_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type contractcontract for which the function is searching in the relating_contractrelating_contract parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified entity name of a type of contract_relationshipcontract_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- contract_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- contract_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the date_time_schema is the definition of dates, both calendar and ordinal, time of day, combinations of date and time of day, and periods of time.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the date_time_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 8 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Any kind of product data may have a date, time, or date and time associated with it.

clause.title: dts_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The dts_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: ahead_or_behind
clause.p:
The ahead_or_behind type is used to specify whether a given time is ahead of coordinated universal time, behind coordinated universal time or is coordinated universal time. NOTENote10.3.2, Note
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes).

dd.p: a given time is ahead of coordinated universal time;
a given time is coordinated universal time;
a given time is behind coordinated universal time.

clause.title: date_time_or_event_occurrence
clause.p: The date_time_or_event_occurrence type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The date_time_or_event_occurrence type allows for the designation of a date_time_selectdate_time_select or an event_occurrenceevent_occurrence.

clause.title: date_time_select
clause.p: The date_time_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
A date_time_select type allows for the designation of a datedate, date_and_timedate_and_time, or a local_timelocal_time.

clause.title: day_in_month_number
clause.p: A day_in_month_number is the position of the specified day in a month.
WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 1 and 31 inclusive.

clause.title: day_in_week_number
clause.p:
A day_in_week_number is the position of the specified day in a week as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote10.3.6, Note
Monday is day number 1, Tuesday is day number 2, Wednesday is day number 3, Thursday is day number 4, Friday is day number 5, Saturday is day number 6, and Sunday is day number 7.
WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 1 and 7 inclusive.

clause.title: day_in_year_number
clause.p: A day_in_year_number is the position of the specified day in a year.

example.p: The 27th day of March is day 86 in years that are not leap years and day 87 in leap years.

clause.p: WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 1 and 366 inclusive.

clause.title: hour_in_day
clause.p: An hour_in_day is the hour element of a specified time on a 24-hour clock. Midnight shall be represented by the value zero.

example.p: The hour_in_day corresponding to 3 o’clock in the afternoon is 15.

note.p: Although ISO 8601 allows two representations for midnight, 0000 and 2400, this part of ISO 10303 restricts the representation to the first value.

clause.p: WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 0 and 23 inclusive.

clause.title: minute_in_hour
clause.p: A minute_in_hour is the minute element of a specified time.
WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 0 and 59 inclusive.

clause.title: month_in_year_number
clause.p:
A month_in_year_number is the position of the specified month in a year as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote10.3.10, Note
January is month number 1, February is month number 2, March is month number 3, April is month number 4, May is month number 5, June is month number 6, July is month number 7, August is month number 8, September is month number 9, October is month number 10, November is month number 11, and December is month number 12.
WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 1 and 12 inclusive.

clause.title: second_in_minute
clause.p: A second_in_minute is the position of the specified second in a minute.

WR1: The value of the real number shall be between 0 to 60.0 inclusive.NOTE 1Note 110.3.11, Note 1
A value of 60 allows for leap seconds. NOTE 2Note 210.3.11, Note 2
The mean solar time is determined by the rotation of the earth. Leap seconds are added as required, usually in the middle or at the end of a year, and ensure that the legal time does not differ from the non-uniform mean solar time by more than one second, in spite of the variations of the earth rotation.

clause.title: week_in_year_number
clause.p:
A week_in_year_number is the position of the specified calendar week as defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote10.3.12, Note
Week number 1 is the week containing the first Thursday of the year. This is equivalent to saying that week number 1 contains the date 4th January.
WR1: The value of the integer shall be between 1 and 53.

clause.title: year_number
clause.p:
A year_number is the year as defined in the Gregorian calendar. The year_number shall be completely and explicitly specified using as many digits as necessary to unambiguously convey the century and year within the century. Truncated year numbers shall not be used. NOTENote10.3.13, Note
ISO 8601:1988 defines the Gregorian calendar.

example.p: The year_number corresponding to the first manned landing on the moon is 1969 (not 69).

clause.p: WR1: The value of the integer shall be greater than 1581.

clause.title: calendar_date
clause.p: A calendar_date is a type of datedate defined as a day in a month of a year as defined in ISO 8601.
day_component: the day element of the datedate.
month_component: the month element of the datedate.

WR1: The entity shall define a valid calendar date.NOTENote10.4.1, Note
If the month_component is ‘April’, ‘June’, ‘August’, or ‘November’ the day_component will be between 1 and 30; when the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_componentyear_component is a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 29; if the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_componentyear_component is not a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 28. Otherwise, the day_component will be between 1 and 31.

clause.title: coordinated_universal_time_offset
clause.p:
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is the oriented offset (specified in hours and possibly minutes) from the coordinated universal time. The offset is defined in ISO 8601 The offset value shall be positive. NOTE 1Note 110.4.2, Note 1
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes). NOTE 2Note 210.4.2, Note 2
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is used to relate a time to coordinated universal time by an offset (specified in hours and minutes) and a direction.
hour_offset: the number of hours by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
minute_offset: the number of minutes by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
sense: the direction of the offset.
actual_minute_offset: the value of the number of minutes offset used to compute the coordinated_universal_time_offset, either the value of minute_offset or 0.
WR1: The hour_offset shall be a positive number, less than 24.
WR2: The minute_offset shall be a positive number, less than or equal to 59.

WR3: If the value of sense specifies that there is no offset from the Coordinated Universal time, hour_offset and actual_minute_offset shall both be equal to zero. If either hour_offset or actual_minute_offset is different from zero, the value of sense shall specify that there is an offset, either ahead or behind, from the Coordinated Universal time.

clause.title: date
clause.p: A date is the identification of a day or week or month in a year. A date may be a calendar_datecalendar_date or an ordinal_dateordinal_date, or a week_of_year_and_day_dateweek_of_year_and_day_date, or a year_monthyear_month. The date is defined in ISO 8601.
year_component: the year in which the date occurs.

clause.title: date_and_time
clause.p: A date_and_time is a moment of time on a particular day.
date_component: the date element of the date time combination.
time_component: the time element of the date time combination.

clause.title: date_role
clause.p:
A date_role is a role for a datedate A date_role is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population related entity data types to form a complete date_role. NOTE 1Note 110.4.5, Note 1
A date_role is a role for a date_assignmentdate_assignment and a description of that role.

name: the labellabel by which the date_role is known.NOTE 2Note 210.4.5, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

description: the texttext that characterizes the date_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.NOTE 3Note 310.4.5, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to date_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each date_role shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 4Note 410.4.5, Note 4
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 5Note 510.4.5, Note 5
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: date_time_role
clause.p:
A date_time_role is a role for a moment of time on a particular day. A date_time_role is an incompletely modeled concept that requires population of related entity data types to form a complete date_time_roleNOTE 1Note 110.4.6, Note 1
A date_time_role is a role for a date_and_time_assignmentdate_and_time_assignment and a description of that role.

name: the labellabel by which the date_time_role is known.NOTE 2Note 210.4.6, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

description: the texttext that characterizes the date_time_role.NOTE 3Note 310.4.6, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to date_time_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each date_time_role shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 4Note 410.4.6, Note 4
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 5Note 510.4.6, Note 5
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: event_occurrence
clause.p:
An event_occurrence is the fact of a transition between states at some point in time. The description of the event_occurrrnece can provide an implicit representation of either the state preceeding the event_occurrence or the state after the event_occurrence. NOTE 1Note 110.4.7, Note 1
The point in time of the existence may not be known in terms of a calendar date before the event_occurrence actually happens. One reason, why the event_occurrence cannot always be expressed as a calendar date, is that the event_occurrence is not possible to plan, for example a break down of a machine.

example.p: The event_occurrence ‘start of production’ implicitly declares that the before the event_occurrence a product was not in production.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the event_occurrence.NOTE 2Note 210.4.7, Note 2
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the event_occurrence is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the event_occurrence. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: event_occurrence_context_role
clause.p: An event_occurrence_context_role establishes a context for an event_occurrence_assignmentevent_occurrence_assignment. An event_occurrence is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete event_occurrence_context_role

example.p: For the event_occurrenceevent_occurrence ‘start of production’ the product, for which production starts, is the context for that event_occurrenceevent_occurrence.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the event_occurrence_context_role is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the event_occurrence_context_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: event_occurrence_relationship
clause.p:
An event_occurrence_relationship is a relationship between two event_occurrenceevent_occurrences with a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 110.4.9, Note 1
The role of event_occurrence_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 210.4.9, Note 2
This entity, together with the event_occurrenceevent_occurrence entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the event_occurrence_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the event_occurrence_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_event: one of the instances of event_occurrenceevent_occurrences that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 3Note 310.4.9, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
