related_event: the other instance of event_occurrenceevent_occurrence. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 4Note 410.4.9, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: event_occurrence_role
clause.p: An event_occurrence_role establishes a role for an event_occurrence. An event_occurrence_role is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete event_occurrence_role
name: the labellabel by which the event_occurrence_role is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the event_occurrence_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: local_time
clause.p:
A local_time is an instance of time represented on a 24-hour clock by hour, minute, and second. The instance is expressed in the local time zone and the offset with the coordinate universal time shall be specified. This concept is defined in ISO 8601. NOTENote10.4.11, Note
This construct is used to represent a moment of time whereas time_measuretime_measure represents amounts of time.
hour_component: the number of hours.
minute_component: the number of minutes. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
second_component: the number of seconds. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
zone: the offset of the local time zone to the coordinated universal time.
WR1: The entity shall define a valid time. The second_component attribute shall only exist if the minute_component attribute exists.

clause.title: ordinal_date
clause.p: An ordinal_date is a type of datedate defined as a day of a year. This concept is defined in ISO 8601.
day_component: the day element of the datedate.
WR1: The day_component shall be between 1 and 365 if the year_componentyear_component is not a leap year. Otherwise the day_component shall be between 1 and 366.

clause.title: relative_event_occurrence
clause.p: A relative_event_occurrence is a type of event_occurrenceevent_occurrence that takes place with an offset to an event_occurrenceevent_occurrence.

example.p: ‘Five days after start of production’ is an example for a relative_event_occurrence, where ‘five days’ is an offset relative to an event_occurrenceevent_occurrence ‘start of production’.

clause.p: base_event: the relative_event_occurrence is defined with respect to the base_event.

offset: the amount of time that passes between the occurrence of the base_event and the relative_event_occurrence. A negative offset specifies that the relative_event_occurrence occurs before the base_event.

clause.title: time_interval
clause.p: A time_interval is the identification of an interval of time. This concept is defined in ISO 8601.

example.p: ‘Strike duration’, ‘delay of production’, and ‘Christmas holidays’ are examples for *time_interval*s.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the time_interval.NOTENote10.4.14, Note
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the time_interval is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the time_interval. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: time_interval_relationship
clause.p:
A time_interval_relationship is a relationship between two time_intervaltime_intervals with a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 110.4.15, Note 1
The role of time_interval_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 210.4.15, Note 2
This entity, together with the time_intervaltime_interval entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the time_interval_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the time_interval_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_time_interval: one of the instances of time_intervaltime_interval that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 3Note 310.4.15, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_time_interval: the other instance of time_intervaltime_interval. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 4Note 410.4.15, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: time_interval_role
clause.p:
A time_interval_role is a role that may be assigned to a time_interval and includes a description of that role. NOTE 1Note 110.4.16, Note 1
The assignment of a role to a time_interval is accomplished by the time_interval_assignment entity data type.
name: the labellabel by which the time_interval_role is known.

description: the texttext that characterizes the time_interval_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.NOTE 2Note 210.4.16, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: time_interval_with_bounds
clause.p: A time_interval_with_bounds is a type of time_intervaltime_interval. The time_interval_with_bounds is bounded either on one side or both sides. If neither secondary_bound nor duration are specified, the time interval begins at the point in time identified by primary_bound and has no specified end point.

example.p: ‘From 01-01-1999 to 31-12-1999’ is an example for a both side bounded time_interval_with_bounds, ‘from 01-01-2000 on’, and ‘until start of production’ are examples for a one side bounded time_interval_with_bounds.

clause.p: primary_bound: one of the bounds of the time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
secondary_bound: the other bound of the time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.

duration: the time_measure_with_unittime_measure_with_unit that specifies the length of a time_interval_with_bounds. If positive, the time_interval_with_bounds is a lower bounded time_interval_with_bounds, else an upper bounded time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
WR1: Either the primary_bound or the secondary_bound or both shall be specified.
WR2: The combination of primary_bound, secondary_bound and duration shall not be specified.
WR3: If primary_bound is specified and secondary_bound is not specified and if duration is specified, the duration shall be positive.
WR4: If primary_bound is not specified and secondary_bound is specified, duration shall be specified and the duration shall be negative.

clause.title: time_role
clause.p:
A time_role is a definition of a role for a local_time. NOTE 1Note 110.4.18, Note 1
The assignment of the role to a local_time is accomplished by the time_assignment entity data type.

name: the labellabel by which the time_role is known.NOTE 2Note 210.4.18, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

description: the texttext that characterizes the time_role.NOTE 3Note 310.4.18, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to time_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994

WR1: Each time_role shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 4Note 410.4.18, Note 4
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 5Note 510.4.18, Note 5
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: week_of_year_and_day_date
clause.p: A week_of_year_and_day_date is a type of datedate defined by identifying the week within a year and the day within that particular week.
week_component: the week element of the datedate.
day_component: the day element of the datedate.
WR1: The result of the expression day_component + (7 * week_componentweek_component) shall be between 1 and 366 if the year_componentyear_component is a leap year.
WR2: The result of the expression day_component + (7 * week_componentweek_component) shall be between 1 and 365 if the year_componentyear_component is not a leap year.

clause.title: year_month
clause.p: A year_month is a type of datedate defined as a month of a year.
month_component: the month element of the datedate.

clause.title: acyclic_event_occurrence_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_event_occurrence_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type event_occurrenceevent_occurrence that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an event_occurrence_relationshipevent_occurrence_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 110.5.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 210.5.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the event_occurrence_relationshipevent_occurrence_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate event_occurrence_relationshipevent_occurrence_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type event_occurrenceevent_occurrence for which the function is searching in the relating_eventrelating_event parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified entity name of a type of event_occurrence_relationshipevent_occurrence_relationship entity.

clause.title: acyclic_time_interval_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_time_interval_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type time_intervaltime_interval that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a time_interval_relationshiptime_interval_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 110.5.2, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 210.5.2, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the time_interval_relationshiptime_interval_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate time_interval_relationshiptime_interval_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type time_intervaltime_interval for which the function is searching in the relating_time_intervalrelating_time_interval parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified entity name of a type of time_interval_relationshiptime_interval_relationship entity.

clause.title: duration_is_positive
clause.p: The duration_is_positive function determines whether a given durationduration is positive. It returns TRUE if the durationduration is a positive. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.
duration: (input) the candidate durationduration that is being checked.

clause.title: duration_is_negative
clause.p: The duration_is_negative function determines whether a given durationduration is negative. It returns TRUE if the durationduration is negative. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.
duration: (input) the candidate durationduration that is being checked.

clause.title: leap_year
clause.p:
The leap_year function checks whether or not a particular year contains 366 days instead of 365 days, known as a leap year. NOTENote10.5.5, Note
Leap years occur every for years.
year: an integer representing a particular year in the Gregorian calendar.

clause.title: valid_calendar_date
clause.p: The valid_calendar_date function determines whether the components of a calendar_datecalendar_date indicate a valid datedate. If the calendar_datecalendar_date is valid, the function returns TRUE. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
date: (input) the candidate calendar_datecalendar_date that is to be checked.

clause.title: valid_time
clause.p: The valid_time function determines whether a candidate local_timelocal_time has a minute_componentminute_component if it has a second_componentsecond_component. It returns FALSE if the condition is not met. Otherwise it returns TRUE.
time: (input) the candidate local_timelocal_time that is to be checked.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- date_time_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- date_time_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the document_schema is the citations of formal standards or documents that are outside the domain of this International Standard. These resource constructs are used to reference additional information that is relevant to the description of the product.

example.p: International, national, and organizational standards, catalogues, and tables of engineering data are examples of formal standards or documents.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the document_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 9 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Product data can include citations of other information sources.

example.p: Heat treatment processes documentation can be specified using the resource constructs that are defined in this schema.

clause.title: product_or_formation_or_definition
clause.p: The product_or_formation_or_definition type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The product_or_formation_or_definition type allows for the designation of a productproduct, a product_definitionproduct_definition, or a product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation.

clause.title: document
clause.p:
A document is an identification of a collection of information. NOTE 1Note 111.4.1, Note 1
The information collected need not be represented in a format conforming to any EXPRESS schema.

example.p: JPEG and HTML files are examples of document.

note.p: This part of ISO 10303 provides several resources to describe documents and to associate them with product data. Annex F.2 provides an explanation about how to describe documents if they are to be considered products.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the document.NOTE 3Note 311.4.1, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 4Note 411.4.1, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

name: the labellabel by which the document is known.NOTE 5Note 511.4.1, Note 5
The name may include the source of the document.

example.p: An example of the source of a document is “ISO”.

clause.p: description: the texttext that characterizes the document. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
kind: the document_typedocument_type that specifies the sort of data that the document describes.
representation_types: the set of document_representation_typedocument_representation_type entities that specifies the way a document is represented.

clause.title: document_product_association
clause.p:
A document_product_association is an association between a documentdocument and a productproduct, between a documentdocument and a product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation, or between a documentdocument and a product_definitionproduct_definition. NOTE 1Note 111.4.2, Note 1
The role of document_product_association can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 211.4.2, Note 2
The document_product_association may establish an equivalence between the documentdocument and the product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation or between the documentdocument and the productproduct of the documentdocument and the product_definitionproduct_definition. This equivalence will provide a document with the versioning structure found in the product_definition_schemaproduct_definition_schema.
name: the labellabel by which the document_product_association is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the document_product_association. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_document: the instance of documentdocument that is part of the association.NOTE 3Note 311.4.2, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_product: the instance of productproduct, product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation, or product_definitionproduct_definition entity data type associated with an instance of documentdocument.NOTE 4Note 411.4.2, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: document_relationship
clause.p:
A document_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type documentdocument and provides a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 111.4.3, Note 1
The role of document_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 211.4.3, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 311.4.3, Note 3
This entity, together with the documentdocument entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the document_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the document_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_document: one of the instances of documentdocument that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 4Note 411.4.3, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_document: the other instance of documentdocument that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 5Note 511.4.3, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: document_representation_type
clause.p: A document_representation_type is a specification of the way a documentdocument is represented.
name: the labellabel by which the document_representation_type is known.

example.p: ‘Digital’ and ‘physical’ are examples for the name.

clause.p: represented_document: the documentdocument for which the kinds of representation are specified.

clause.title: document_type
clause.p:
A document_type is the kind of data that a formal standard or document may provide information about. NOTENote11.4.5, Note
The applicable values of document_type can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘Material’, ‘surface finish’, and ‘heat treatment process’ are all pieces of data that can be described implicitly, by reference to other documents (such as standards documents), rather than explicitly every time they are used.

clause.p: product_data_type: the name of the kind of data contained in a document.

example.p: ‘Material description’ is an example of product_data_type that characterizes the information provided by a standards document for material.

clause.title: document_usage_constraint
clause.p:
A document_usage_constraint is an identification of a specific subject area or aspect from within a document and gives the relevant information or text that applies. The semantics of the reference can be found in the documentdocument itself. NOTE 1Note 111.4.6, Note 1
This entity could be used to identify the clause of a document and the content or portions of the content in that clause that are relevant.

source: the documentdocument in which the subject_element originates.NOTE 2Note 211.4.6, Note 2
The inverse of this relationship is used to define multiple elements of a documentdocument.
subject_element: the name of an element of the source.
subject_element_value: the labellabel that conveys a specific value of the subject_element present in the source

example.p: For references to a ‘surface finish’ source the subject_element may be a ‘Clause 2.1 surface imperfection’ and its associated subject_element_value may be ‘no visible imperfections’, ‘no more than two imperfections that are more than 0.06 inch diameter within any given square inch of surface area’, or ‘no imperfections under 10 times magnification’.

clause.title: document_with_class
clause.p: A document_with_class is a type of documentdocument for which a classification is specified.

example.p: A surface finish document may be identified by various classes, class A, class B, and class C. Each class of surface finish specifies various allowances for imperfections in the surface finish. Class A may require no visible imperfections, class B may require no more than two imperfections that are more than 0.06 inch diameter within any given square inch of surface area, and class C may require no imperfections under 10 times magnification.

clause.p:
class: the identification of the data classification to which the documentdocument belongs.NOTENote11.4.7, Note
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: The value of this attribute would be ‘A’, ‘B’ or ‘C’ in the previous example.

clause.title: acyclic_document_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_document_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type documentdocument that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a document_relationshipdocument_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 111.5.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 211.5.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the document_relationshipdocument_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate document_relationshipdocument_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type documentdocument for which the function is searching in the relating_documentrelating_document parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the document_relationshipdocument_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- document_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- document_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the effectivity_schema is the validity of aspects of product data or product life cycle activity data specified against certain criteria.
This schema supports the representation of effectivity according to the following criteria:

li.p: selection of a given batch of product data;
selection of product data by serial number;
selection of product data by a date.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the effectivity_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 10 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Effectivity information can be attached to any aspect of product data or product life cycle activity data.
Only effectivities based on date, serial number, and lot number are considered in this schema.

clause.title: effs_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The effs_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: effs_name_attribute_select
clause.p: The effs_name_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: condition
clause.p: A condition is a type of action_methodaction_method that must be fulfilled before a statement or relationship becomes valid.

clause.title: conditional_effectivity
clause.p: A conditional_effectivity is a type of conditioncondition or effectivityeffectivity for which the domain of applicability is defined by an explicit condition.

clause.title: conditional_configuration
clause.p: A conditional_configuration is a type of conditional_effectivityconditional_effectivity and represents an association of a product_concept_feature_associationproduct_concept_feature_association object with a design or process in order to define a valid usage of it in the context of a certain product_classproduct_class.
configuration_type: the configuration_type defines the valid usage of a conditional_configuration.
inheritance_type: the inheritance_type specifies the inheritance scheme for the configuration information as either exception, inherited, or local.

li.p: An exception inheritance_type is when no inheritance scheme is applicable and all required configuration information must be attached locally at the business object.

An inherited inheritance_type is when a scheme for inheritance of configuration information applies. The complete configuration information shall be collected from the different levels in the structure by evaluation of results.

A local inheritance_type is when no inheritance scheme is applicable and all required configuration information must be attached locally at the business object. Nevertheless, any potentially inherited configuration information of a higher level shall be consistent, i.e., it shall be a subset of the locally defined configuration information.

clause.title: dated_effectivity
clause.p: A dated_effectivity is a type of effectivityeffectivity for which the domain of applicability is defined as a possibly open-ended interval of time.

effectivity_end_date: the date_time_or_event_occurrencedate_time_or_event_occurrence that defines the upper bound of the interval of applicability. If a value for this attribute is not defined, the interval of applicability has no upper limit.

effectivity_start_date: the date_time_or_event_occurrencedate_time_or_event_occurrence that defines the lower bound of the interval of applicability. If a value for this attribute is not defined, the interval of applicability has no lower limit.
WR1: One or both of the effectivity_start_date or effectivity_end_date shall be specified.

clause.title: effectivity
clause.p: An effectivity is the identification of a domain of applicability for product data.

example.p: A process is effective from 1998 March 1 through 1998 December 31.

clause.p: An effectivity may be either a serial_numbered_effectivityserial_numbered_effectivity or a dated_effectivitydated_effectivity, or a lot_effectivitylot_effectivity, or a time_interval_based_effectivitytime_interval_based_effectivity.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the effectivity.NOTE 1Note 112.4.5, Note 1
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 212.4.5, Note 2
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

name: the labellabel by which the effectivity is known.NOTE 3Note 312.4.5, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to effectivity as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

description: the texttext that characterizes the effectivity.NOTE 4Note 412.4.5, Note 4
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to effectivity as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each effectivity shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 5Note 512.4.5, Note 5
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

WR2: Each effectivity shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.NOTE 6Note 612.4.5, Note 6
The name_attributename_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 7Note 712.4.5, Note 7
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: effectivity_relationship
clause.p:
An effectivity_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type effectivityeffectivity with a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 112.4.6, Note 1
The role of effectivity_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 212.4.6, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 312.4.6, Note 3
This entity, together with the effectivityeffectivity entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the effectivity_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the effectivity_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

related_effectivity: the other instance of effectivity that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 4Note 412.4.6, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

relating_effectivity: one of the instances of effectivityeffectivity that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 5Note 512.4.6, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: lot_effectivity
clause.p: A lot_effectivity is a type of effectivityeffectivity for which the domain of applicability is defined as a given batch of items.
effectivity_lot_id: the identification of the batch of items.
effectivity_lot_size: the size of the batch of items.

clause.title: serial_numbered_effectivity
clause.p:
A serial_numbered_effectivity is a type of effectivityeffectivity for which the domain of applicability is defined as a possibly open-ended interval of serial numbers. NOTENote12.4.8, Note
A serial number is represented in this International Standard as an identifier. It is supposed here that, regardless of their format, identifiers used to represent serial numbers are ordered.
effectivity_start_id: the first valid serial number.
effectivity_end_id: the last valid serial number. If a value for this attribute is not defined, the interval of applicability has no upper bound.

clause.title: time_interval_based_effectivity
clause.p:
A time_interval_based_effectivity is a type of effectivityeffectivity for which the domain of applicability is defined as a time_intervaltime_interval. NOTENote12.4.9, Note
This entity data type provides greater functionalities than the entity data type dated_effectivitydated_effectivity. In particular, it allows the specification of an effectivity period in which the period of time is defined by a date and a duration.
effectivity_period: the time_intervaltime_interval defining the period of time when the associated product data are effective.

clause.title: acyclic_effectivity_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_effectivity_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type effectivityeffectivity that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a effectivity_relationshipeffectivity_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 112.5.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 212.5.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the effectivity_relationshipeffectivity_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate effectivity_relationshipeffectivity_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type effectivityeffectivity for which the function is searching in the relating_effectivityrelating_effectivity parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified entity name of a type of effectivity_relationshipeffectivity_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- effectivity_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- effectivity_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the experience_schema is the identification and characterization of types of experience or particular episodes of experience gained by persons. This schema provides for the definition of generic data relating to particular episodes of experience.

example.p: The identification of a particular episode of experience is an example of generic data relating to experience.
The identification of a particular type of experience is an example of generic data relating to experience.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the experience_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 11 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: This schema provides resources for the identification, naming, and description of:

clause.title: experience
clause.p: An experience is an episode of practice, undertaken by a person or organization, that contributes to the accumulation of knowledge or a skill.

example.p: 100 flying hours in a Tornado jet undertaken by a particular pilot in a particular year.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the experience.NOTE 1Note 113.3.1, Note 1
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 213.3.1, Note 2
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

name: the labellabel by which the experience is known.NOTE 3Note 313.3.1, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
description: the texttext that characterizes the experience. The value of this attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: experience_relationship
clause.p: An experience_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the experienceexperience entity data type and provides for the identification, naming, and description of that relationship.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the experience_relationship.NOTE 1Note 113.3.2, Note 1
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 213.3.2, Note 2

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the external_reference_schema is the means of identifying information that is not explicitly represented in a given exchange.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the external_reference_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 12 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Product data may refer to information that is not explicitly represented in a given exchange. This information is either predefined, in the annotated EXPRESS schema to which the exchange conforms, or is defined elsewhere. If the information is defined in the annotated EXPRESS schema to which the exchange conforms, this requirement is satisfied by a reference that identifies the entity data type definitions in the annotated EXPRESS schema. Otherwise, this requirement is satisfied by a reference that identifies the record type definitions and exchange format.

clause.title: ers_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The ers_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: message
clause.p:
A message is a communication that is addressed to a system in order to trigger some action. The result of such an action is an external item or identification. NOTENote14.3.2, Note
The role of message can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

sourcecode.body: TYPE message = STRING; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE message = STRING; END_TYPE;

clause.title: source_item
clause.p: The source_item type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
A source_item type allows for the designation of an identifieridentifier or a messagemessage.

clause.title: external_source
clause.p:
An external_source is the identification of a source of product data that is not the EXPRESS schema to which the exchange conforms. NOTE 1Note 114.4.1, Note 1
The product data may conform to some other part of this International Standard.
source_id: the identification of the external_source.

description: the texttext that characterizes the external_source.NOTE 2Note 214.4.1, Note 2
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to external_source as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each external_source shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 3Note 314.4.1, Note 3
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 4Note 414.4.1, Note 4
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

An external_source_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type external_sourceexternal_source with a description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 114.4.2, Note 1
The role of external_source_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: One external_sourceexternal_source may be a subset of another external_sourceexternal_source. This entity may be specialized to specify such a relationship.

note.p: This entity, together with the external_sourceexternal_source entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3

item_id: the string that specifies the identification of the referent item.
source: an external_sourceexternal_source that contains the referent item.

This entity, together with the externally_defined_itemexternally_defined_item entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

references: a list of source_itemsource_items defining a path to the target item_iditem_id.

The item_iditem_id inherited from the externally_defined_itemexternally_defined_item is the target for the reference list, but is excluded from the list itself. The list ends at a entity data type that explicitly references the target or that is explicitly referenced by the target.

example.p: A reference to the colour ‘red’ without any definition of the associated red-green-blue values would be a pre_defined_item if the red-green-blue values of the colour ‘red’ were specified in the relevant annotated EXPRESS schema.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the group_schema is the definition of groups of items.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Groups are collections of product data that have a common identity. Any kinds of product data may be grouped together. The structure specified in this schema enables the common identity to be captured; it does not specify, or allow the specification of, the meaning of the common identity or the criteria for the common identity.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the language_schema specifies the data structure for the representation of language support.

li.p: IP1: The name attribute of the language shall be an alpha-3 bibliographic code of ISO 639-2.
IP2: If present, the description attribute shall identify a country with an alpha-2 code specified in ISO 3166-1.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the language_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 14 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: This specifies the representation of the language used in text attributes and the association of translations to these texts.

clause.title: language
clause.p: A language is a type of groupgroup that is a specification of the language in which an information is given. The group shall specify in its name a language code according to ISO 639-2, and, if present, in its description a country code according to ISO 3166-1.
Informal proposition
WR1: The name attribute of the language shall be specified.

sourcecode.body: END_SCHEMA; -- language_schema
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- language_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the location_schema is the identification and characterization of different representations of places or positions in space at which something can take place or exist.

example.p: The identification of a geographical location is an example of generic data relating to a location.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the location_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 15 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: This schema provides resources for the identification, naming, and description of:

clause.title: location
clause.p:
A location is a place or position in space at which something can take place or exist. NOTENote17.3.1, Note
The specification or representation of a location might take the form of a postal address, a set of geographical or spacial coordinates, or an association with a product.

example.p: A map reference specifies a location where a building exists.
The “bridge” of a particular ship specifies a location where navigation equipment should be installed.

clause.p: id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the location.
name: the labellabel by which the location is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the location. The value of this attribute need not be specified.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the management_resources_schema is the association of management data with other aspects of product data in specific application contexts.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the management_resources_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 16 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p:
The relationship between management type data and other aspects of product data is application-specific. Management data may be assigned to various kinds of product data. The assignment of management data can be defined in a generic manner and then specialized according to each considered application context. NOTENote18.2, Note
In the following definitions, the expression “assigned product data” means “the product data that are referenced by subtypes of the generic abstract supertypes of this schema”. Use of these generic constructs is defined in annex E.5.

clause.title: mrs_role_select
clause.p: The mrs_role_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

sourcecode.body: TYPE mrs_role_select = SELECT BASED_ON role_select WITH (action_assignment, action_request_assignment, approval_assignment, certification_assignment, contract_assignment, document_reference, effectivity_assignment, external_referent_assignment, group_assignment, name_assignment, security_classification_assignment); END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE mrs_role_select = SELECT BASED_ON role_select WITH (action_assignment, action_request_assignment, approval_assignment, certification_assignment, contract_assignment, document_reference, effectivity_assignment, external_referent_assignment, group_assignment, name_assignment, security_classification_assignment); END_TYPE;

clause.title: assignment_object_select
clause.p:
The assignment_object_select type is an extensible list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to instances of the data types included in the types that extend the assignment_object_select type.NOTENote18.3.2, Note
This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.

sourcecode.body: TYPE assignment_object_select = EXTENSIBLE SELECT; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE assignment_object_select = EXTENSIBLE SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: attribute_type
clause.p: The attribute_type type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The attribute_type data type allows for the designation of a label or a text that can be assigned to an attribute of an entity.

clause.title: action_assignment
clause.p: An action_assignment is an association of an actionaction with product data.
assigned_action: the instance of the actionaction entity data type that is to be associated with product data.

role: the object_roleobject_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the action_assignment with product data.NOTE 1Note 118.4.1, Note 1
This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of action_assignment using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each action_assignment shall be the item_with_roleitem_with_role in at most one role_associationrole_association.NOTE 2Note 218.4.1, Note 2
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: action_method_assignment

description: the texttext that characterizes the action_method_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: attribute_value_assignment
clause.p: An attribute_value_assignment is an extendion of the cardinality of a string valued attribute in an entity data type by one. The relationship of the extension to the existing attribute is determined by the role. The entity data types that have the attribute for which the extension is provided are identified by a specialization of attribute_value_assignmentattribute_value_assignment.

attribute_name: the attribute for which the additional value is defined. The attribute_name shall identify an attribute of the assigned entity.NOTE 1Note 118.4.8, Note 1
The identified attribute may be defined in the entity or inherited from a supertype.

example.p: ‘name’ and ‘description’ are examples for the attribute_name.

clause.p: attribute_value: the attribute_typeattribute_type that contains, as labellabel, the additional value for the attribute of the assigned entity specified by attribute_name.

role: the attribute_value_roleattribute_value_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the attribute_value_assignment with product data.NOTE 2Note 218.4.8, Note 2
The values related to this attribute can be specified in an annotated EXPRESS schema that uses or specializes this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.p: description: the texttext that characterizes the attribute_value_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: external_referent_assignment
clause.p:
An external_referent_assignment is an identification of product data referenced in outside sources.NOTE 1Note 118.4.31, Note 1
This is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete external_referent_assignment.

example.p: A URI for an externally defined tool is specified by assigning the value ‘http://www.tool.com/mill.stp’ to the name attribute of external_referent_assignment. The fact that the value is a URI is established by assigning a value of ‘uri’ to the role attribute of external_referent_assignment.

A URI fragment identifier for the bottom face of the externally defined tool is specified by assigning the value ‘http://www.tool.com/mill.stp#bottom_face’ to the name attribute of external_referent_assignment. The fact that the value is a URI

clause.p:
assigned_name: the labellabel by which the external_referent_assignment is known.NOTE 2Note 218.4.31, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

role: the object_roleobject_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the external_referent_assignment with product data.NOTE 3Note 318.4.31, Note 3
This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of external_referent_assignment using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each external_referent_assignment shall be the item_with_roleitem_with_role in at most one role_associationrole_association.NOTE 4Note 418.4.31, Note 4

clause.title: identification_assignment_relationship

An identification_assignment_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type identification_assignmentidentification_assignment and provides an identification and description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 118.4.34, Note 1
The role of identification_assignment_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 218.4.34, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 318.4.34, Note 3
This entity, together with the identification_assignmentidentification_assignment entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the identification_assignment_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the identification_assignment_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_identification_assignment: one of the instances of identification_assignmentidentification_assignment that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 4Note 418.4.34, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: acyclic_assignment_object_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_assignment_object_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type assignment_object_selectassignment_object_select that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an assignment_object_relationshipassignment_object_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTENote18.5.1, Note
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
relation: (input) the candidate assignment_object_relationshipassignment_object_relationship to be checked.

specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the assignment_object_relationshipassignment_object_relationship entity.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the measure_schema is the description of physical quantities.

example.p: Density, length, force, and time are different kinds of physical quantities.

clause.p: The resource constructs defined in this schema are based upon material in ISO 31 and ISO 1000.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the measure_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
:: ISO -
See Annex D, Paragraph 17 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following requirements are supported by this schema:

li.p: it shall be possible to specify the predefined kinds of physical quantity if the kind of a physical quantity is known at the time when the schema is being specified;
it shall be possible to specify non-predefined kinds of physical quantity if the kind of a physical quantity is not known at the time when the schema is being specified.

example.p: The elements of a list of material properties are physical quantities. Each element may be a different kind of physical quantity. The kind of each element is only decided upon at instantiation time.

note.p: ISO 1000 gives “kilogram” as the SI unit name. This part of ISO 10303 uses “gram” as the SI unit name.

clause.title: solid_angle_measure
clause.p: A solid_angle_measure is the value of a solid angle.

sourcecode.body: TYPE solid_angle_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE solid_angle_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;

clause.title: thermodynamic_temperature_measure
clause.p: A thermodynamic_temperature_measure is the value for the degree of heat of a body.

sourcecode.body: TYPE thermodynamic_temperature_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE thermodynamic_temperature_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;

clause.title: time_measure
clause.p: A time_measure is the value of the duration of a period.

sourcecode.body: TYPE time_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE time_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;

clause.title: unit
clause.p: The unit type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

A unit is a physical quantity, with a value of one. NOTENote19.3.45, Note
A unit is used to express other physical quantities of the same kind.

clause.title: velocity_measure
clause.p: A velocity_measure is the value of the rate of change of position.

sourcecode.body: TYPE velocity_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE velocity_measure = REAL; END_TYPE;

clause.title: volume_measure

clause.title: absorbed_dose_measure_with_unit
clause.p: An absorbed_dose_measure_with_unit is a type of measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit in which the physical quantity is an absorbed dose of radiation as defined in ISO 31.
WR1: The unit_componentunit_component be of type absorbed_dose_unitabsorbed_dose_unit.

clause.p: An absorbed_dose_unit is a type of derived_unitderived_unit in which the absorbed dose is expressed.
WR1: The dimensional exponents shall be equal to those of the Gray as defined in ISO 31.

WR1: The dimensional exponent of length shall be equal to one, the dimensional exponent of time shall be equal to minus two, and all the other dimensional exponents shall be equal to zero.

clause.title: amount_of_substance_measure_with_unit
clause.p: An amount_of_substance_measure_with_unit is a type of measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit. // in which the physical quantity is an This entity data type shall only be used to characterize a number of particles.
WR1: The unit shall be an amount_of_substance_unitamount_of_substance_unit.

clause.title: amount_of_substance_unit
clause.p:
An amount_of_substance_unit is a type of named_unitnamed_unit in which the number of elementary entities of a substance as compared to the number of atoms in 0.012 kilograms of carbon-12 is expressed. NOTE 1Note 119.4.10, Note 1
This definition applies to the SI quantity ‘mole’. When the mole is used, the elementary entities, whose quantity is expressed, must be specified. They may be atoms, molecules, ions, electrons or other particles or specified groups of such particles (see ISO 31-8). NOTE 2Note 219.4.10, Note 2
This unit corresponds to one of the seven fundamental quantities as specified in ISO 1000.

sourcecode.body:
ENTITY amount_of_substance_unit
  SUBTYPE OF (named_unit);
WHERE
  WR1: ((((((SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.length_exponent = 0.0) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.mass_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.time_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.electric_current_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.thermodynamic_temperature_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.amount_of_substance_exponent = 1.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.luminous_intensity_exponent = 0.0);
END_ENTITY;

amed_unit.dimensions.length_exponent = 0.0) AND (SELF

amed_unit.dimensions.time_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.electric_current_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.thermodynamic_temperature_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.amount_of_substance_exponent = 1.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.luminous_intensity_exponent = 0.0);
END_ENTITY;

clause.p: WR1: The dimensional exponent of amount of substance shall be equal to one, and all the other dimensional exponents shall be equal to zero.

clause.title: area_measure_with_unit

WR1: The unit shall be an area_unitarea_unit.

clause.p: An area_unit is a type of derived_unitderived_unit used to measure the extent of a surface.

clause.title: celsius_temperature_measure_with_unit

clause.title: context_dependent_unit
clause.p: A context_dependent_unit is a type of named_unitnamed_unit that is not related to the system of units defined in this part of ISO 10303.

example.p: The number of parts in an assembly is a physical quantity that may be measured in a unit called “parts”. Such a unit cannot be related to an SI unit.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the context_dependent_unit is known.

clause.title: conversion_based_unit
clause.p:
A conversion_based_unit is a type of named_unitnamed_unit that defines a unit on the basis of a measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit. NOTENote19.4.15, Note
The value_componentvalue_component attribute of the measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit defines the conversion factor.

example.p: An inch is a conversion_based_unit. It is from the Imperial system, its name is “inch”, and it can be related to the si_unitsi_unit, millimetre, through a measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit whose value is 25.4 millimetre. A foot is also a conversion_based_unit. It is from the Imperial system, its name is “foot”, and it can be related to an si_unitsi_unit, millimetre, either directly or through the unit called “inch”.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the conversion_based_unit is known.
conversion_factor: the measure_with_unitmeasure_with_unit that specifies the physical quantity from which the conversion_based_unit is derived.
WR1: The dimensional exponents shall be equal to those from the conversion_factorconversion_factor.

clause.title: derived_unit
clause.p: A derived_unit is an expression of units.

example.p: Newtons per square millimetre is a derived_unit.

clause.p: A derived_unit may be either an absorbed_dose_unitabsorbed_dose_unit or an acceleration_unitacceleration_unit, or a radioactivity_unitradioactivity_unit, or an area_unitarea_unit, or a capacitance_unitcapacitance_unit, or a dose_equivalent_unitdose_equivalent_unit, or an electric_charge_unitelectric_charge_unit, or a conductance_unitconductance_unit, or an electric_potential_unitelectric_potential_unit, or an energy_unitenergy_unit, or a magnetic_flux_density_unitmagnetic_flux_density_unit or a force_unitforce_unit, or a frequency_unitfrequency_unit, or an illuminance_unitilluminance_unit, or an inductance_unitinductance_unit, or a magnetic_flux_unitmagnetic_flux_unit, or a power_unitpower_unit, or a pressure_unitpressure_unit, or a resistance_unitresistance_unit, or a velocity_unitvelocity_unit, or a volume_unitvolume_unit.
elements: the derived_unit_elementderived_unit_elements and their exponents that define the derived_unit.

name: the label by which the derived_unit is known.NOTE 1Note 119.4.16, Note 1
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to derived_unit as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.
WR1: There shall be either more than one member in the elements set or the value of the exponent of the single element of the elements set shall not be equal to one.

WR2: Each derived_unit shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.NOTE 2Note 219.4.16, Note 2
The name_attributename_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 3Note 319.4.16, Note 3
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: derived_unit_element
clause.p:
A derived_unit_element is the association of a named_unitnamed_unit with an exponent. NOTENote19.4.17, Note
This entity is used in this part of ISO 10303 to represent an element of the dimensional expression of a derived_unitderived_unit.

example.p: Newtons per square millimetre is a derived unit. It has two elements, Newton whose exponent has a value of 1, and millimetre whose exponent is -2.

clause.p: unit: the named_unitnamed_unit that specifies the mathematical factor of the element.
exponent: the power that is applied to the unit attribute.

clause.title: dimensional_exponents
clause.p:
A dimensional_exponents is a definition of the powers of the dimensions of the seven base quantities. NOTE 1Note 119.4.18, Note 1
The seven base quantities are defined in ISO 31. NOTE 2Note 219.4.18, Note 2
This entity enables the dimensional expression of any physical quantity with respect to these seven base quantities. NOTE 3Note 319.4.18, Note 3
Length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity are the seven base quantities.

example.p: A length of 2 millimetres has a length exponent of 1. The remaining exponents are equal to 0.
A velocity of 2 millimetres per second has a length exponent of 1 and a time exponent of -1. The remaining exponents are 0.

clause.p: length_exponent: the power of the length base quantity.
mass_exponent: the power of the mass base quantity.
time_exponent: the power of the time base quantity.
electric_current_exponent: the power of the electric current base quantity.
thermodynamic_temperature_exponent: the power of the thermodynamic temperature base quantity.
amount_of_substance_exponent: the power of the amount of substance base quantity.
luminous_intensity_exponent: the power of the luminous intensity base quantity.

sourcecode.body:
ENTITY electric_current_unit
  SUBTYPE OF (named_unit);
WHERE
  WR1: ((((((SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.length_exponent = 0.0) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.mass_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.time_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.electric_current_exponent = 1.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.thermodynamic_temperature_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.amount_of_substance_exponent = 0.0)) AND (SELF
amed_unit.dimensions.luminous_intensity_exponent = 0.0);
END_ENTITY;

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the person_organization_schema is the description of information that identifies people and organizations.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the person_organization_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 18 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: People and organizations are associated with product data to provide data concerning administrative structures and individuals who serve as points of contact or have particular responsibility in those structures. People and organizations may be associated with any aspect of product data.

clause.title: person_organization_select
clause.p: The person_organization_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The person_organization_select type allows for the designation of an organizationorganization, a personperson or a person_and_organizationperson_and_organization.

clause.title: pos_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The pos_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

sourcecode.body: TYPE pos_description_attribute_select = SELECT BASED_ON description_attribute_select WITH (person_and_organization_role, person_and_organization, person_role, organization_role, organizational_project); END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE pos_description_attribute_select = SELECT BASED_ON description_attribute_select WITH (person_and_organization_role, person_and_organization, person_role, organization_role, organizational_project); END_TYPE;

clause.title: address
clause.p:
An address is the information necessary for communicating, using one or more communication methods. NOTE 1Note 120.4.1, Note 1
In addition to the attributes defined in address additional generic attributes may be assigned using generic_attribute_assignmentgeneric_attribute_assignment.

example.p: A generic attribute named “LinkedIn” with a value of “Fred.Bloggs” could be used to add a LinkedIn account to address information.

clause.p: internal_location: an organization-defined address for internal mail delivery. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
street_number: the number of a location on a street. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
street: the name of a street. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
postal_box: the number of a postal box. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
town: the name of a town. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
region: the name of a region. The value of this attribute need not be specified.

example.p: The counties of Great Britain and the states of the United States of America are examples of regions.

clause.p: postal_code: the code that is used by the country‘s postal service. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
country: the name of a country. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
facsimile_number: the number at which facsimiles may be received. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
telephone_number: the number at which telephone calls may be received. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
electronic_mail_address: the electronic address at which electronic mail may be received. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
telex_number: the number at which telex messages may be received. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
name: the labellabel that specifies the name of the location identified by the address.

example.p: “White House”, “Buckingham Palace”, “Kremlin”.

clause.p:
url: the text that specifies the uniform resource locator associated with the address.NOTE 2Note 220.4.1, Note 2
The format of uniform resource locators is defined in IETF RFC 1738 [4].

example.p: URLs are used to identify items such as world wide web sites and file transfer protocol (FTP) servers.

clause.p:
WR1: At least one of the attributes shall have a value.NOTE 3Note 320.4.1, Note 3
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: organization

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_definition_schema is the identification of products, the categorization of products, definitions of products, and the relationships among them. This schema provides for the generic aspects of product definition.

example.p: The identification of products and definitions of products, the grouping of products according to classification schemes and the definition of various kinds of relationship between products are all examples of generic aspects of product definition.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the product_definition_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
See Annex D, Paragraph 19 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The use of the entity data types of this schema to represent products is specified in the viewpoint as defined by the requirements of an annotated EXPRESS schema that uses or specializes this part of ISO 10303. Every product need not be represented by an instance of the entity data type product. Some products may be represented by other constructs in the integrated resources.

example.p: The constructs product_definition_formation and product_definition, defined in the product_definition_schema of this part of ISO 10303, are examples of other entity data types that may represent a product.
The construct action_resource, defined in ISO 10303-49, is an example of an entity data type that may represent a product.

clause.p: A single product may have multiple groups of definitions associated with it; each group is valid in a given application context.

example.p: An application context may be the manufacture of ball-point pens. A particular design of ball-point pen has multiple versions. Each version is described through a group of product definitions. An older version has a solid cap whereas a more recent version has a hole in the cap to prevent people from choking if they swallow it. The characteristics of the two versions would be different from each other because the later version would have a hole in the cap whereas the earlier version would not. This schema could be used to define the ball-point pen with a solid cap as one product and the one with a hole in the cap as another. On the other hand it could also be used to define both pens as two versions of a single product. The approach taken would depend upon the requirements of the application context.

clause.p: The definition of a product may include the properties that characterize it.

example.p: An integrated circuit product will have a functional definition represented by a circuit schematic diagram and a physical definition represented by a circuit layout diagram.

clause.p: Definitions of products may be related to each other in various ways. This part of ISO 10303 provides the resources needed to identify the relationships among products and to be able to characterize those relationships.

example.p: The ball-point pen cap would be related in an assembly relationship to the ball-point pen itself and one of the caps could be substituted for the other in some circumstances.

clause.p: There are two ways to represent the concept of real object:

li.p: a real object can be represented by an instance of product if the subject of an annotated Express schema is concerned with real objects or if it is needed to describe a real object at various life-cycle stages and in various configurations; in this case, if an real object is identified by a serial number, this serial number can be stored in the id attribute of the product;

example.p: An airplane, in service during 30 years, may have different configurations during its life.

li.p: a real object can be represented by an instance of product_definition if the subject of an annotated Express schema is primarily concerned with the design phase of products and if the concept of real object is considered as a particular stage in the design phase of a product; in this case, if a real object is identified by a serial number, this serial_number can be stored in the id attribute of the product_definition.

example.p: A prototype may be considered as a particular definition of a product.

clause.p:
Product definition facts are independent of properties. The ways in which these facts may be combined are prescribed by the relationships that are defined in this schema. Each product definition fact can be interpreted in any application context; the ways in which these facts are to be interpreted are prescribed in annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialise the resources defined in this part of ISO 10303.NOTENote21.2, Note
An example of the way in which this schema may be used is given in annex F.1.

clause.title: product_definition_or_reference
clause.p:
