This empty extensible select requires extension in a further schema to ensure that entities that refer to it have at least one valid instantiation.

clause.title: source
clause.p: The source type is a list of alternate choices that enables one to characterize whether a product is to be manufactured within an organization, bought, or the fact that this information is not known.

dd.p: characterize a product is to be manufactured within an organization;
characterize a product is to be bought;
information, whether a product is to be manufactured within an organization or bought, is not known.

clause.p: An alternative_solution_relationship is a product_definition_formation_relationshipproduct_definition_formation_relationship that specifies the type of the relationship.

clause.title: characterized_product
clause.p:
A characterized_product is a type of characterized_objectcharacterized_object and a type of productproduct for the purpose of characterizing a product. NOTENote21.4.2, Note
Properties that are assigned using characterized_object are outside version control, whereas properties added via product_definition are under version control.

clause.title: generic_product_definition_reference
clause.p: A generic_product_definition_reference is a reference to an externally defined product_definitionproduct_definition that may or may not have a local representation. A generic_product_definition_reference is either a product_definition_referenceproduct_definition_reference or a product_definition_reference_with_local_representationproduct_definition_reference_with_local_representation.
source: defines the location which contains the original definition of the product_definitionproduct_definition.

clause.title: product
clause.p:
A product is a representation of a product or a type of product NOTE 1Note 121.4.4, Note 1
The term product is defined in ISO 10303-1.

example.p: The SS Titanic is a product that could be represented by product.
Lifeboat is a class of products that could be represented by the entity data type product. Each lifeboat on the SS Titanic is a member of this class.
The computer used to edit this document, the Eiffel Tower, and coal are examples of products existing in the real world.
A company develops a new lawnmower, a product that will be realized through a manufacturing and assembly process.
Heating, lighting, and Internet connectivity are examples of functions.

A company may develop a generic engine that is described by a schematic drawing showing its main principles and components. This product may be used as the basis for a range of engines that share characteristics such as multi-valve and operating temperature. Then, when defining a new engine, designers create a specialization of this generic engine with specific characteristics such as cylinder volume and power.

note.p: The products or classes of products that are represented by product are specified in annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product.NOTE 4Note 421.4.4, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 5Note 521.4.4, Note 5
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

example.p: Part numbers, stock item numbers, and serial numbers are examples of product identifiers.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the product is known.

example.p: ‘Widget’ is an example of name.

clause.p: description: the texttext that characterizes the product. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
frame_of_reference: a set of product_contextproduct_context entities that defines the contexts within which the data associated with the product is relevant.

clause.title: product_category
clause.p: A product_category is a classification that applies to products.

example.p: In an application protocol whose context includes manufactured parts, ‘mechanical part’, ‘electrical part’, ‘structural part’, ‘piping part’, ‘water pipe’, and ‘hot water pipe’ are examples of types of product.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the product_category is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_category. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_category.NOTE 1Note 121.4.5, Note 1
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to product_category as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994. NOTE 2Note 221.4.5, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 3Note 321.4.5, Note 3
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

WR1: Each product_category shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.NOTE 4Note 421.4.5, Note 4
The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 5Note 521.4.5, Note 5
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: product_category_relationship
clause.p:
A product_category_relationship is a hierarchical relationship of one category with another and provides a description of their relationship. If a productproduct belongs to a product_categoryproduct_category, it also belongs to all of the parent categories.NOTE 1Note 121.4.6, Note 1
The role of product_category_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: The two sub-level product_categoryproduct_categorys called ‘cold water pipe’ and ‘hot water pipe’ can be related to each other through the more generic product_categoryproduct_category called ‘piping part’ by using two product_category_relationships, one product_category_relationship between ‘piping part’ and ‘cold water pipe’ and the other product_category_relationship between ‘piping part’ and ‘hot water pipe’.

note.p: Networks of instances of product_categoryproduct_category may be defined using this entity.

example.p: A product_categoryproduct_category called ‘piping part’ may be the parent category of sub-categories called ‘cold water pipe’ and ‘hot water pipe’. The product_categoryproduct_category called ‘hot water pipe’ may be a sub-category of another product_categoryproduct_category called ‘boiler output pipe’. This is an example of a product_categoryproduct_category network because the product_categoryproduct_category called ‘hot water pipe’ has two parents.

note.p: This entity, in conjunction with the product_categoryproduct_category entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the product_category_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_category_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
category: the parent of the sub_category.

example.p: In the previous example, ‘piping part’ would be the category for ‘cold water pipe’ and ‘hot water pipe’.

clause.p: sub_category: a child of the category.

example.p: In the previous example ‘cold water pipe’ would be the sub_category for ‘piping part’ in one case and ‘hot water pipe’ would be the sub_category in the other.

clause.p: WR1: A graph of product_categoryproduct_category instances shall not be cyclic.

clause.title: product_definition
clause.p:
A product_definition is a representation of an aspect of a product, or of a class of products, for an identified life cycle stage. The life cycle stage for which a product_definition exists may be further characterized by discipline, by usage, or by both. NOTE 1Note 121.4.7, Note 1
The product_definition entity type supports the representation of different views of a product for different purposes. Multiple views of the same product, or class of products, are represented by different instances of product_definition for the same product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation.

example.p: The design of the SS Titanic and the as-built description of the SS Titanic can be represented as two instances of product_definition for the product that represents the ship itself.

clause.p: The product_definition entity data type may represent particular products that are the members of an identified class of products.

example.p: Each individual lifeboat on the SS Titanic can be represented by an instance of product_definition, in which the associated productproduct represents the class of products whose members are the lifeboats.

note.p: A product_definition can identify an occurrence of a product.

clause.p: The product_definition entity data type acts as an aggregator for information about the properties of products.

example.p: The designed shape of an aeroplane can be identified by an instance of the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape entity data type that is associated with the design product_definition of the aeroplane.

clause.p: The usage of a product_definition in another context is specified through its participation in a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship as the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition in which the using context is specified by the frame_of_reference of the relating_product_definitionrelating_product_definition.

If a product_definition is considered in multiple contexts, the product_definition_context_associationproduct_definition_context_association shall be used to specify a collection of product_definition_contextproduct_definition_contexts.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_definition.NOTE 3Note 321.4.7, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 4Note 421.4.7, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
formation: the product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation to which the product_definition relates.
frame_of_reference: the product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context in which the product_definition is defined.

name: the labellabel by which the product_definition is known.NOTE 5Note 521.4.7, Note 5
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to product_definition as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

WR1: Each product_definition shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.NOTE 6Note 621.4.7, Note 6
The name_attributename_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 7Note 721.4.7, Note 7
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: product_definition_context_association
clause.p:
A product_definition_context_association is an association of a product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context with a product_definitionproduct_definition, and specifies the meaning of this association.NOTE 1Note 121.4.8, Note 1
A product_definition_context_association may be used to associate a using context to a product_definitionproduct_definition. The defining context is associated to the product_definitionproduct_definition using frame_of_referenceframe_of_reference.

example.p: A product_definitionproduct_definition, initially defined in the context of ‘mechanical design’, and in which the representation of the shape of a product is defined, may also be relevant in the context of ‘process-planning design’. For such a case, the product_definition_context_association would relate the product_definitionproduct_definition with the product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context characterizing the context ‘process-planning design’ and the name of the role attribute would be ‘other relevant context’.

clause.p: definition: the reference to a product_definitionproduct_definition associated to a context.
frame_of_reference: the product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context that defines the stage in the product life cycle with which the product_definitionproduct_definition is to be associated.

role: the product_definition_context_roleproduct_definition_context_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the context of this frame_of_reference attribute with the product_definitionproduct_definition of the definition attribute.NOTE 2Note 221.4.8, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: product_definition_context_role
clause.p: A product_definition_context_role is a specification of the purpose of a product_definition_contextproduct_definition_context.
name: the labellabel by which the product_definition_context_role is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_context_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: product_definition_effectivity
clause.p:
A product_definition_effectivity is a type of effectivityeffectivity. A product_definition_effectivity is the identification of a valid use of a particular product_definitionproduct_definition in the context of its participation in a given product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship. The referenced product_definitionproduct_definition is the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition attribute of the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship.NOTENote21.4.10, Note
Appropriate subtypes of product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship and further information about the way to describe assemblies are specified in ISO 10303-44.
usage: the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship that defines the context of the effectivityeffectivity.
WR1: A product_definition_effectivity shall not be referred to as assigned_effectivityassigned_effectivity.

clause.title: product_definition_formation
clause.p: A product_definition_formation is a collector of definitions of a product.

example.p: An application interpreted model could use this entity to support the identification of different versions of a single productproduct. Each version would be described by a group of instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition and each group, identified by a product_definition_formation, would be associated with the same productproduct.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_definition_formation.NOTE 1Note 121.4.11, Note 1
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

example.p: Part version number is an example of a product_definition_formation identifier.

clause.p:
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_formation. The value of the attribute need not be specified.NOTE 2Note 221.4.11, Note 2
This attribute may be used to depict differences in the purpose and function of different formations of a single productproduct.

of_product: the productproduct to which the product_definition_formation belongs.NOTE 3Note 321.4.11, Note 3
A productproduct is associated with one or more product_definition_formation instances through the implicit inverse of this relationship.

clause.title: final_solution
clause.p: A final_solution is a type of product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation and is a set of additional sensual characteristics that can be applied to an occurrence that represents a neutral part in order to complete its definition.
status: the text string that describes the level of completion between the neutral part and the final part.
specification: the set of instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition that defines the various aspects of the final_solution.

clause.title: product_definition_formation_relationship
clause.p:
A product_definition_formation_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation and provides an identification and description of this relationship.NOTE 1Note 121.4.13, Note 1
A relationship may exist between instances of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that relate to different instances of the entity data type productproduct or between different formations of the same productproduct. NOTE 2Note 221.4.13, Note 2
The role of product_definition_formation_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 3Note 321.4.13, Note 3
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 4Note 421.4.13, Note 4
This entity, together with the product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_definition_formation_relationship.NOTE 5Note 521.4.13, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 6Note 621.4.13, Note 6
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the product_definition_formation_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_formation_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_product_definition_formation: one of the instances of product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 7Note 721.4.13, Note 7
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_product_definition_formation: the other instance of product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent up on the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 8Note 821.4.13, Note 8
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: product_definition_formation_with_specified_source
clause.p: A product_definition_formation_with_specified_source is a type of product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation whose source is identified to be either manufactured within an organization, bought, or the fact that this information is not known.
make_or_buy: the characterization of the source of the product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation.

clause.title: product_definition_relationship
clause.p:
A product_definition_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition or generic_product_definition_referencegeneric_product_definition_reference and provides an identification and description of this relationship.NOTE 1Note 121.4.15, Note 1
A relationship may exist between instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition that relate to different instances of the entity data type productproduct or between different definitions of the same productproduct.

example.p: The relationships within a bill-of-materials structure are examples of product_definition_relationship entity data types that associate different productproducts. The relationship between a sketch and a detailed design is an example of a product_definition_relationship that associates different definitions of a single productproduct.

note.p: A single product_definitionproduct_definition may be used more than once within the description of a productproduct.

example.p: The same component could be used more than once in the same assembly. Each usage of the component would be specified as an instance of the product_definition_relationship entity.

note.p: The role of product_definition_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the product_definitionproduct_definition entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_definition_relationship.NOTE 6Note 621.4.15, Note 6
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 7Note 721.4.15, Note 7
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the product_definition_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_product_definition: one of the instances of product_definitionproduct_definition that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 8Note 821.4.15, Note 8
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 9Note 921.4.15, Note 9
In the context of an ISO 10303 application protocol, the product_definition_relationship is an assembly component relationship, the relating_product_definition may be the assembly.

related_product_definition: the other instance of product_definitionproduct_definition that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 10Note 1021.4.15, Note 10
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 11Note 1121.4.15, Note 11
In the context of an ISO 10303 application protocol, the related_product_definition may be the product_definitionproduct_definition that is an element of the assembly.

clause.title: product_definition_relationship_relationship
clause.p: A product_definition_relationship_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_definition_relationship_relationship.
name: the labellabel by which the product_definition_relationship_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_relationship_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
relating: one of the instances of product_definitionproduct_definition that is a part of the relationship.

related: the other instance of product_definitionproduct_definition that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

clause.title: product_definition_reference
clause.p: A product_definition_reference is a type of generic_product_definition_referencegeneric_product_definition_reference that identifies the externally defined product_definitionproduct_definition by providing the key attributes necessary to unambiguously identify it and the associated product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation, productproduct and organization that owns the product id.

product_id: specifies the identifier of the externally defined product, where the referenced product_definitionproduct_definition is assigned to one of its product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation.
product_definition_formation_id: specifies the identifier of the externally defined product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation.
product_definition_id: specifies the identifier of the externally defined product_definitionproduct_definition.
id_owning_organization_name: specifies the id owner of the externally defined product, realised by an applied organization_assignmentorganization_assignment with the role ‘id owner’.

clause.title: product_definition_reference_with_local_representation
clause.p: A product_definition_reference_with_local_representation is a type of generic_product_definition_referencegeneric_product_definition_reference that represents an externally defined product_definitionproduct_definition by a local product_definitionproduct_definition.

clause.title: product_definition_substitute
clause.p:
A product_definition_substitute is an association of a product_definitionproduct_definition with a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship. The association states the fact that the product_definitionproduct_definition may replace, in the context of the relationship, the product_definitionproduct_definition that is specified in the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition attribute of the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship.NOTE 1Note 121.4.19, Note 1
If a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship exists between a component part and its assembly, a product_definition_substitute could be used to capture an allowable substitute, that is, a different component part that may be used as a replacement in the same assembly.

example.p: Two kinds of ball-point pens may be manufactured: a standard model and a deluxe model. Each model of the pen would be specified as a separate product_definitionproduct_definition related to a particular kind of nib: a standard nib and a deluxe nib, respectively. The fact that the deluxe nib and the standard nib are interchangeable only in the context of the standard model of ball-point pen is established with this construct.

clause.p: description: the texttext that characterizes the product_definition_substitute. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
context_relationship: the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship that specifies the context in which the replacement may occur.

example.p: In the previous example, the relating_product_definitionrelating_product_definition of a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship identified as a context_relationship would be the standard model of the ball-point pen and the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition would be the standard nib.

clause.p: substitute_definition: the product_definitionproduct_definition that acts as an allowed replacement for the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition of the context_relationship.

example.p: In the previous example, this attribute would identify the deluxe nib .

clause.p:
name: the labellabel by which the product_definition_substitute is known.NOTE 2Note 221.4.19, Note 2
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to product_definitionproduct_definition as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.
WR1: A product_definitionproduct_definition shall not be defined as a substitute for itself.

WR2: Each product_definition_substitute shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.NOTE 3Note 321.4.19, Note 3
The name_attributename_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303 NOTE 4Note 421.4.19, Note 4
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: product_definition_with_associated_documents
clause.p: A product_definition_with_associated_documents is a type of product_definitionproduct_definition in which the associated documents participate in the definition of the product.
documentation_ids: the set of instances of documentdocument entity data type that are associated with the product_definitionproduct_definition.

clause.title: product_related_product_category
clause.p: A product_related_product_category is a type of product_categoryproduct_category that identifies products that satisfy the type identified by the category.
products: a set of productproducts that belong to the product_related_product_category.

clause.title: product_relationship
clause.p:
A product_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type productproduct and provides an identification and description of their relationship.NOTE 1Note 121.4.22, Note 1
The role of product_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 221.4.22, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 321.4.22, Note 3
This entity, together with the productproduct entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the product_relationship.NOTE 4Note 421.4.22, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the product_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the product_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_product: one of the instances of productproduct that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 5Note 521.4.22, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_product: the other instance of productproduct that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent up on the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 6Note 621.4.22, Note 6
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: acyclic_alternative_solution_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_alternative_solution_relationship function determines whether the graph of instance of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. this function may be used to evaluate either a alternative_solution_relationshipalternative_solution_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTENote21.5.1, Note
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
relation: (input) the candidate alternative_solution_relationshipalternative_solution_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation for which the function is searching in the relating_product_definition_formationrelating_product_definition_formation parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the alternative_solution_relationshipalternative_solution_relationship entity.

clause.title: acyclic_product_category_relationship
clause.p:
The acyclic_product_category_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type product_categoryproduct_category that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a product_category_relationshipproduct_category_relationship or any of its subtypes. The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTENote21.5.2, Note
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
relation: (input) the candidate product_category_relationshipproduct_category_relationship to be checked.
children: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type product_categoryproduct_category that the function is searching for in the category field of the relation argument.

clause.title: acyclic_product_definition_formation_relationship
clause.p:
The acyclic_product_definition_formation_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a product_definition_formation_relationshipproduct_definition_formation_relationship or any of its subtypes. The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 121.5.3, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 221.5.3, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the product_definition_formation_relationshipproduct_definition_formation_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate product_definition_formation_relationshipproduct_definition_formation_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation that the function is searching for in the relating_product_definition_formationrelating_product_definition_formation parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the product_definition_formation_relationshipproduct_definition_formation_relationship entity.

clause.title: acyclic_product_definition_relationship
clause.p:
The acyclic_product_definition_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship or any of its subtypes. The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 121.5.4, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 221.5.4, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship to be checked.

relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type product_definitionproduct_definition that the function is searching for in the relating_product_definitionrelating_product_definition parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship entity.

clause.title: acyclic_product_relationship
clause.p:
The acyclic_product_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type productproduct that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a product_relationshipproduct_relationship or any of its subtypes. The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 121.5.5, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 221.5.5, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the product_relationshipproduct_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
relation: (input) the candidate product_relationshipproduct_relationship to be checked.
relatives: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type productproduct that the function is searching for in the relating_productrelating_product parameter of the relation argument.
specific_relation: (input) the fully qualified entity name of a type of product_relationshipproduct_relationship entity.

clause.title: categories_of_product
clause.p: The categories_of_product function returns the set of product category names associated with the argument. The function evaluates the bag of instances of product_categoryproduct_category that are associated with the input productproduct through an instance of product_related_product_categoryproduct_related_product_category. The function returns the SET of STRING values stored in the namename attribute of the instances of product_categoryproduct_category in the bag.
obj: the productproduct whose categories are searched.

clause.title: get_product_definitions
clause.p:
The get_product_definitions function returns for any instance of productproduct the set of instances of product_definitionproduct_definition that refer to the product through an instance of product_definition_formationproduct_definition_formation. NOTENote21.5.7, Note
This function is not used in this schema.
c_def_instance: the candidate productproduct to be checked.

sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: END_SCHEMA; -- product_definition_schema

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_property_definition_schema is the characteristics of an object.

This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the product_property_definition_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:
:: ISO -
:: ISO -
:: ISO -
:: ISO -
See Annex D, Paragraph 20 for a graphical representation of this schema.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: This schema provides resources for the identification of:

li.p: types of properties to be identified and described;
properties assigned to a characterized_object, a product_definition, a product_definition_relationship or a shape_definition.

clause.p: The meaning of each assigned property may be defined either by its association with an instance of the entity characterizing a type of property or by its name attribute.

example.p: The definition of the surface finish of a shape is independent of the way in which the shape or the surface finish is represented.

note.p: In the previous example, both the defined surface finish and the shape could have multiple representations.

clause.p: Each characteristic may be associated with a single characterized_object or product_definition or with one product_definition in the context of another. Each characteristic is independent of the number or types of representations of that characteristic. Each characteristic may be associated with the shape of a product, an element of the shape of a product, or the relationship between elements of the shape of a product.
This part of ISO 10303 distinguishes between the definition of a product and its possible usages. This part of ISO 10303 establishes the following assumptions:

li.p: the definition of a given object is characterized by a set of unique properties.

example.p: A product cannot have two shapes simultaneously.

li.p: any usage of the object is characterized by a set of unique properties.

example.p: A product, like glue, may have different shapes depending on its usage.

li.p: a property characterizes either the definition or one of the usages of an object.

example.p: The appearance of chair x is a unique property of that chair. The colour designating that the chair is white is a single item in a representation for the appearance property of chair x. This colour is shareable among many representations for the properties of many different objects.

clause.title: characterized_definition
clause.p: The characterized_definition type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The characterized_definition type allows for the designation of a characterized_objectcharacterized_object, a characterized_product_definitioncharacterized_product_definition, a characterized_itemcharacterized_item or a shape_definitionshape_definition to which properties may be assigned.

clause.title: characterized_item
clause.p: The characterized_item type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The characterized_item type allows for the designation of an item_identified_representation_usageitem_identified_representation_usage, a dimensional_sizedimensional_size, or a geometric_tolerancegeometric_tolerance to which properties may be assigned.

clause.title: ppds_id_attribute_select
clause.p: The ppds_id_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: characterized_product_definition
clause.p: The characterized_product_definition type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The characterized_product_definition type allows for the designation of a product_definitionproduct_definition, or a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship, or a product_definition_relationship_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship_relationship, or a product_definition_occurrenceproduct_definition_occurrence to which properties may be assigned.

Selection of a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship means that the property is applied to the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition attribute in the context of its relating_product_definitionrelating_product_definition attribute. Selection of a product_definition_relationship_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship_relationship means that the property is applied to the relatedrelated attribute in the context of its relatingrelating attribute.NOTENote22.3.4, Note
This enables properties of a given product that depend on the usages of this product to be described.

example.p: The shape of a gasket depends upon whether or not it is an element of an assembly and, if it is an element of an assembly, the shape depends upon the assembly in which it participates.

clause.title: derived_property_select
clause.p: The derived_property_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The derived_property_select type allows for the selection of an action_propertyaction_property, a property_definitionproperty_definition, or a resource_propertyresource_property, or a dimensional_locationdimensional_location, or a dimensional_sizedimensional_size, or a geometric_tolerancegeometric_tolerance.

sourcecode.body: TYPE derived_property_select = SELECT (property_definition, action_property, resource_property, dimensional_location, dimensional_size, geometric_tolerance); END_TYPE;
sourcecode.fmt-sourcecode: TYPE derived_property_select = SELECT (property_definition, action_property, resource_property, dimensional_location, dimensional_size, geometric_tolerance); END_TYPE;

clause.title: shape_aspect_or_characterized_object
clause.p: The shape_aspect_or_characterized_object type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: shape_definition
clause.p: The shape_definition type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.
The shape_definition type allows for the designation of a product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape, a shape_aspectshape_aspect, or a shape_aspect_relationshipshape_aspect_relationship.
References to a shape_aspect_relationshipshape_aspect_relationship are references to the relationship itself and not to one of the associated shape_aspectshape_aspect.

clause.title: internal_or_reflected_shape_aspect
clause.p: The internal_or_reflected_shape_aspect type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: multi_or_next_assembly_usage_occurrence
clause.p: The multi_or_next_assembly_usage_occurrence type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

clause.title: characterized_object
clause.p:
A characterized_object is the identification of an item that has associated property information. NOTE 1Note 122.4.1, Note 1
A characterized_object is characterized by the properties which refer to it. NOTE 2Note 222.4.1, Note 2
The properties of a characterized_object may be used as an environmental condition under which the properties of a product are measured.

example.p: If a product has a set of properties that are measured within a room or an atmosphere, the room or atmosphere may be described with instances of the entity data type characterized_object.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the characterized_object is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the characterized_object. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: characterized_object_relationship
clause.p:
A characterized_object_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type characterized_objectcharacterized_object and provides an identification and description of this relationship. NOTE 1Note 122.4.2, Note 1
The role of characterized_object_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 222.4.2, Note 2
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed. NOTE 3Note 322.4.2, Note 3
This entity, together with the characterized_objectcharacterized_object entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
name: the labellabel by which the characterized_object_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the characterized_object_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_object: one of the instances of characterized_objectcharacterized_object that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 4Note 422.4.2, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_object: the other instance of characterized_objectcharacterized_object that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 5Note 522.4.2, Note 5
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: component_path_shape_aspect
clause.p: A component_path_shape_aspect is a type of shape_aspectshape_aspect that identifies a portion of a shape of an assembly by referencing a shape_aspectshape_aspect that represents a portion of the shape of an occurrence of a part within this assembly. The referenced part and its shape_aspectshape_aspect might be defined locally or externally.
location: the occurrence of a part by its next_assembly_usage_occurrencenext_assembly_usage_occurrence or multi_level_reference_designatormulti_level_reference_designator.

component_shape_aspect: the locally or externally defined shape_aspectshape_aspect. In the case that it is externally defined, only the idid of the externally defined shape_aspectshape_aspect is provided.

clause.title: constituent_shape_aspect
clause.p: A constituent_shape_aspect is a type of shape_aspectshape_aspect that identifies a portion of a shape_aspectshape_aspect.
parent: the shape_aspectshape_aspect of which this entity is an aspect.
of_shape: the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape of which this entity is an aspect.

clause.title: general_property
clause.p:
A general_property is an identification of a type of property. NOTE 1Note 122.4.5, Note 1
An annotated Express schema can use this entity to identify a property selected in a library of properties. NOTE 2Note 222.4.5, Note 2
If needed, a general_property may be a member of a group.

example.p: “Kinematic viscosity”, defined in ISO 31, is an example of a general_property.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the general_property.NOTE 3Note 322.4.5, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 4Note 422.4.5, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the general_property is known.

example.p: ‘Kinematic viscosity’ is an example of name.

clause.p: description: the texttext that characterizes the general_property. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: general_property_association
clause.p: A general_property_association is an association of an instance of one of the types listed in derived_property_selectderived_property_select with a general_propertygeneral_property. The general_propertygeneral_property serves as the reference definition for the considered property.

example.p: In order to characterize the kinematic viscosity of a fluid, an instance of general_property_association would relate an instance of general_propertygeneral_property that defines the concept of kinematic viscosity and an instance of property_definitionproperty_definition that defines the kinematic characteristics of an instance of product_definitionproduct_definition defining the fluid.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the general_property_association is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the general_property_association. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
base_definition: the general_propertygeneral_property that provides the definition of the considered characteristic.
derived_definition: the derived_property_selectderived_property_select, for which the identification of the considered characteristic is provided by a general_propertygeneral_property.

WR1: In the case that the derived_definition is of type property_definitionproperty_definition, action_propertyaction_property or resource_propertyresource_property it shall be referred to by at most one general_property_association.

WR2: In the case that the derived_definition is of type property_definitionproperty_definition, action_propertyaction_property or resource_propertyresource_property the attribute name of the derived_definition shall be the same as the attribute name of the base_definition.

clause.title: general_property_relationship
clause.p:
A general_property_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type general_propertygeneral_property and provides an identification and description of this relationship. NOTE 1Note 122.4.7, Note 1
This entity, together with the general_propertygeneral_property entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3

name: the labellabel by which the general_property_relationship is known.NOTE 2Note 222.4.7, Note 2
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
description: the texttext that characterizes the general_property_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_property: one of the instances of general_propertygeneral_property that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 3Note 322.4.7, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

related_property: the other instance of general_propertygeneral_property that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 4Note 422.4.7, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: product_definition_shape
clause.p:
A product_definition_shape is a type of property_definitionproperty_definition. It identifies the shape of an object. A product_definition_shape identifies the shape of a characterized_objectcharacterized_object or of one of the types reachable as characterized_product_definitioncharacterized_product_definition. NOTE 1Note 122.4.8, Note 1
A product_definition_shape need not be associated with any geometric representation. NOTE 2Note 222.4.8, Note 2
Early in the design of a product there may not be a specific idea about the shape of the product but there may be certain characteristics of the shape that are to be represented. Those product shape characteristics can be attached to the product shape using this entity.

example.p: A geometric representation of shape is not needed to assert facts such as, “a shape must fit within a 5 centimetre cube”.

clause.p: WR1: The definition attribute shall not refer to a shape_definitionshape_definition.

clause.title: property_definition
clause.p:
A property_definition is a property that characterizes a single object. NOTE 1Note 122.4.9, Note 1
The type of the characterized item is one of the entity types that may be selected directly or indirectly with characterized_definitioncharacterized_definition. NOTE 2Note 222.4.9, Note 2
The role of property_definition can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
name: the labellabel by which the property_definition is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the property_definition. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
definition: the item whose property is identified.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the property_definition.NOTE 3Note 322.4.9, Note 3
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to property_definition as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994. NOTE 4Note 422.4.9, Note 4
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 5Note 522.4.9, Note 5
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

WR1: Each property_definition shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.NOTE 6Note 622.4.9, Note 6
The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in support_resource_schemasupport_resource_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 7Note 722.4.9, Note 7
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the support_resource_schemasupport_resource_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: shape_aspect
clause.p:
A shape_aspect is an identified element of the shape of an object or is part of another shape_aspect. NOTE 1Note 122.4.10, Note 1
A shape_aspect that is part of another shape_aspect allows decomposition of a shape_aspect.

example.p: Consider the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape of a bolt. One might distinguish, as an element of this shape, the concept of the threaded portion of its shank. This portion of the shape could be specified using a shape_aspect entity so that other properties, such as surface finish, may be associated with it.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the shape_aspect is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the shape_aspect. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
of_shape: the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape of which this entity is an aspect.

example.p: If the identified aspect is the threaded portion of a bolt’s shank; this attribute would be the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape of the bolt.

clause.p: product_definitional: an indication that the shape_aspect is on the physical boundary of the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape. If the value of this attribute is TRUE, the shape_aspect being identified is on such a boundary. If the value is FALSE, the shape_aspect being identified is not on such a boundary. If the value is UNKNOWN, it is not known whether or not the shape_aspect being identified is on such a boundary.

example.p: If the identified shape_aspect is the threaded portion of a bolt’s shank, the value of this attribute would be TRUE. If it is the centre-line, the value would be FALSE.

clause.p:
id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the shape_aspect.NOTE 2Note 222.4.10, Note 2
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to shape_aspect as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994. NOTE 3Note 322.4.10, Note 3
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 4Note 422.4.10, Note 4
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

WR1: Each shape_aspect shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.NOTE 5Note 522.4.10, Note 5
The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 6Note 622.4.10, Note 6
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: shape_aspect_occurrence
clause.p: A shape_aspect_occurrence is a type of shape_aspectshape_aspect that is defined by another shape_aspectshape_aspect or a characterized_objectcharacterized_object.
definition: the shape_aspectshape_aspect or characterized_objectcharacterized_object that is defining this shape_aspect_occurrence.
WR1: In the case that a shape_aspect_occurrence is defined by another shape_aspect_occurrence, the graph established by the attribute definitiondefinition shall not be cyclic.

clause.title: shape_aspect_relationship
clause.p:
A shape_aspect_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type shape_aspectshape_aspect and provides an identification and description of their relationship. NOTE 1Note 122.4.12, Note 1
The role of shape_aspect_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 222.4.12, Note 2
If one shape_aspectshape_aspect is part of another, this entity could be used to associate the two shape_aspectshape_aspects. NOTE 3Note 322.4.12, Note 3
Each shape_aspectshape_aspect entity may have different properties. NOTE 4Note 422.4.12, Note 4
No actual physical relationship is established between related instances of the entity data type shape_aspectshape_aspect.

example.p: A shape_aspect_relationship might relate two instances of the entity data type shape_aspectshape_aspect whose representations are the equivalent surfaces of a mould and a moulded product. The shape of the mould is not spatially related to the moulded product.

note.p: Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the shape_aspectshape_aspect entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the shape_aspect_relationship is known.
description: the texttext that characterizes the shape_aspect_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

relating_shape_aspect: one of the instances of shape_aspectshape_aspect that is a part of the relationship.NOTE 7Note 722.4.12, Note 7
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A shape_aspectshape_aspect with five faces would play the role of relating_shape_aspect in five instances of the entity data type shape_aspect_relationship: one per face.

clause.p:
related_shape_aspect: the other instance of shape_aspectshape_aspect that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.NOTE 8Note 822.4.12, Note 8
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

id: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the shape_aspect_relationship.NOTE 9Note 922.4.12, Note 9
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to shape_aspect_relationship as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994. NOTE 10Note 1022.4.12, Note 10
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 11Note 1122.4.12, Note 11
The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

WR1: Each shape_aspect_relationship shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.NOTE 12Note 1222.4.12, Note 12
The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303. NOTE 13Note 1322.4.12, Note 13
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the product_property_representation_schema is the representation of properties.
The requirements addressed by this schema are:

li.p: the ability to associate a representation with a property_definition that it represents;
the ability to identify a representation as representing a shape;

the ability to identify relationships between the representations of shapes and to state that the identified relationships are the representations of zero, one or more instances of the entity data type product_definition.

clause.p: This clause defines the information requirements to which implementations shall conform using the EXPRESS language as defined in ISO 10303-11. The following EXPRESS declaration begins the product_property_representation_schema and identifies the necessary external references.
Short names of entities defined in this schema are described in Annex A. Unambiguous identification of this schema is defined in Annex B.

note.p: The schemas referenced above are specified in the following parts:

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following assumptions apply to the product_property_representation_schema:

li.p: this International Standard will include various types of representations ranging from simple collections of geometry to more elaborate collections of representations of different kinds of properties;
it is possible to have more than one representation of a single property;
a single representation may be used to represent a property of zero, one, or many instances of the entity data type product_definition;
any property of a product_definition is an identifiable concept independent of how, or even if, it is represented.

note.p: Representation schemas are defined in other parts of ISO 10303. This schema provides a structure within which these resources can be brought together to represent the properties of a product.

clause.title: pprs_description_attribute_select
clause.p: The pprs_description_attribute_select type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The chained_representation_link type allows for the designation of a mapped_itemmapped_item, a representation_contextrepresentation_context, or a representation_relationshiprepresentation_relationship.

clause.title: represented_definition
clause.p: The represented_definition type is a list of alternate data types. It provides a mechanism to refer to an instance of one of these data types.

The represented_definition type allows for the designation of a general_propertygeneral_property, a property_definitionproperty_definition, a property_definition_relationshipproperty_definition_relationship, a shape_aspectshape_aspect, or a shape_aspect_relationshipshape_aspect_relationship.

clause.title: chain_based_item_identified_representation_usage
clause.p: A chain_based_item_identified_representation_usage is a type of item_identified_representation_usageitem_identified_representation_usage that represents a chain of representations in a graph of representations, where the undirected links in the graph can be instances of entity data types representation_contextrepresentation_context, representation_relationshiprepresentation_relationship, or mapped_itemmapped_item. The directed links are derived from the nodes and undirected links and consist solely of instances of the entity data type representation_relationshiprepresentation_relationship. The attribute rep_2rep_2 of the derived instances is directed towards the root, while the attribute rep_1rep_1 is directed towards the leaf.
nodes: the list of representationrepresentation in the chain.

undirected_link: the list of items that relate nodes in the chain.NOTE 1Note 123.4.1, Note 1
The items in the undirected_link are placed correctly relative to the nodes in the chain but are not guaranteed to have a consistent direction along the chain.
root: the node that is the initial terminus of the chain.
leaf: the node that is the final terminus of the chain.
directed_link: the list of representation_relationshiprepresentation_relationship that are derived from the undirected_link and that are consistently directed from the root to the leaf.

WR1: The directed_linkdirected_link attribute shall be valid for the given set of nodesnodes and undirected_linkundirected_links.NOTE 2Note 223.4.1, Note 2
the get_directed_linkget_directed_link function returns indeterminate if it cannot construct a valid list. The EXPRESS EXISTS function returns FALSE with an indeterminate input.

nodes: the list of representationrepresentation in the chain.

undirected_link: the list of items that relate nodes in the chain.NOTE 1Note 123.4.2, Note 1
The items in the undirected_link are placed correctly relative to the nodes in the chain but are not guaranteed to have a consistent direction along the chain.
root: the node that is the initial terminus of the chain.
leaf: the node that is the final terminus of the chain.
directed_link: the list of representation_relationshiprepresentation_relationship that are derived from the undirected_link and that are consistently directed from the root to the leaf.

WR1: The directed_linkdirected_link attribute shall be valid for the given set of nodesnodes and undirected_linkundirected_links.NOTE 2Note 223.4.2, Note 2

clause.title: context_dependent_shape_representation
clause.p:
A context_dependent_shape_representation is the association of a shape_representation_relationshipshape_representation_relationship with a product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape. The product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape identifies the shape of a product_definitionproduct_definition as it plays the role of the related_product_definitionrelated_product_definition in a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship. NOTE 1Note 123.4.4, Note 1
The role of context_dependent_shape_representation can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A gasket’s shape depends upon whether the gasket is participating in an assembly relationship and, if it is a part of an assembly, the product or products with which it is assembled.
The position of a bolt’s shape depends upon the way it is positioned in a given assembly.

clause.p: representation_relation: a shape_representation_relationshipshape_representation_relationship that is associated with the product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape.

represented_product_relation: a product_definition_shapeproduct_definition_shape that identifies the shape of the related product_definitionproduct_definition in the context of a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship.

WR1: The represented_product_relation shall identify the shape of a product_definition_relationshipproduct_definition_relationship.

WR2: Each context_dependent_shape_representation shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.NOTE 4Note 423.4.4, Note 4
The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

WR3: Each context_dependent_shape_representation shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.NOTE 5Note 523.4.4, Note 5

clause.title: item_identified_representation_usage
clause.p: An item_identified_representation_usage is an identification of a single or a set or a list of representation_itemrepresentation_item(s) within a representationrepresentation as being the element(s) that describes a particular component or part of the property that is described by the representationrepresentation. More than one representationrepresentation. may be bound to a product data item by members of item_identified_representation_usage and more than one member of representation_itemrepresentation_item(s) may be bound to a product data item by members of item_identified_representation_usage. The same item of product data shall not be bound to more than one member of representation_itemrepresentation_item within a member of representationrepresentation.

example.p: In an application protocol, an instance of representation describes the shape of a product. One element of the representationrepresentation — a curve — represents the boundary of a shape_aspect, a hole, in the product. Item_identification_representation_usage is used to state that the curve referenced by ‘identified_item’ is a representation item for the shape_aspect referenced by ‘definition’ and that the whole representation is referenced by ‘used_representation’ to indicate the structural context for the curve. Geometric_representation_context plays no role in this example.

In an application protocol, an instance of representation describes the shape of a product. One element of the representationrepresentation — a curve — represents the boundary of a shape_aspect, a hole, in the product. A member of Item_identification_representation_usage is used to state that the curve referenced by ‘identified_item’ is a representation item for the shape_aspect#1 referenced by ‘definition’ and that the whole representation is referenced by ‘used_representation’ to indicate the structural context for the curve. A second member of Item_identification_representation_usage references a different curve in that same representationrepresentation and references the same shape_aspect#1. The data population is invalid because only one item within a representation can be bound to a shape_aspect.

clause.p: name: the labellabel by which the item_identified_representation_usage is known.

definition: the general_propertygeneral_property, property_definitionproperty_definition, property_definition_relationshipproperty_definition_relationship, shape_aspectshape_aspect, or shape_aspect_relationshipshape_aspect_relationship that is represented.

used_representation: the representationrepresentation that describes the property or aspect of which the definition is a part or component, and that contains the identified_item (directly or indirectly) as one of its items.

identified_item: the representation_itemrepresentation_item or list_representation_itemlist_representation_item or set_representation_itemset_representation_item that describes the identified property or aspect.
WR1: If the size of identified_itemidentified_item is one then the used_representationused_representation shall reference the item directly or indirectly.

WR2: If the size of identified_itemidentified_item is greater than one then the used_representationused_representation shall be one of the representationrepresentations that reference the item directly or indirectly.
